trackers.name: RMN — Accélérer la conservation dans le sud du Québec (ACSQ), $144 million
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a $144 million Québec programme aimed at southern Québec — the part of the province where biodiversity is both richest and most threatened. Four streams, and the shape of them matters: $100 MILLION for conserving natural areas INCLUDING THE ACQUISITION OF PRIVATE LAND, by real right or by conservation servitude; $8.65 million for knowledge-building and awareness work on sites of interest WITH A VIEW TO EVENTUAL ACQUISITION; and $870,000 to help owners get natural reserves recognised. WHO IT SUITS: Québec conservation organisations and their partners, with explicit intent to work more closely with the Indigenous conservation movement. HOW IT DIFFERS: the knowledge stream funds the survey and case-building BEFORE a purchase — so a site you cannot yet afford to buy can still be worked up now.

trackers.name: The Nature Trust of British Columbia
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a non-profit land conservation organisation that BUYS ecologically significant private land in BC and manages it — more than 500 parcels acquired since 1971, over 180,000 acres (73,000 ha) protected, with regional land managers stationed across the province. Carries no debt and no mortgages. USE IT: the strategic point is the inverse of what you might expect. Only about 6% of BC's land base is privately owned — but a DISPROPORTIONATE share of at-risk species and ecosystems sit in the low valley bottoms and coastal lowlands where that private land is concentrated. So a small privately-held parcel in a valley bottom can matter far more than its size suggests, and it is exactly the kind of site the Trust assembles into larger conservation complexes with partners and government.

trackers.name: Land Trust Alliance of British Columbia (LTABC)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the provincial alliance representing around 35 land trust members across British Columbia (roughly 100 including associate members — consultants, environmental groups and individuals). Founded 1997. BC land trusts have between them protected well over a million acres. USE IT: LTABC takes direct approaches — its own invitation is to TALK TO THEM ABOUT A PROPERTY YOU WOULD LIKE TO PROTECT THROUGH A LAND DONATION OR CONSERVATION COVENANT — so you do not need to identify the right member trust yourself; start here and be routed. Its published guidance is unusually practical, including Greening Your Title, a guide to conservation covenants, and Green Legacies on planned giving, which is the route when a landowner wants to leave land protected rather than sell it now. Its news coverage extends to Alberta as well as BC.

trackers.name: HCTF Habitat Acquisition Grants — money to buy private land (BC)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: grants of $100,000 and up to LAND TRUSTS, COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS AND FIRST NATIONS to PURCHASE private property protecting fish and wildlife habitat in British Columbia. One intake a year, deadline in April. WHO IT SUITS: know where the money comes from, because it decides what gets funded — the grant is paid for by LICENCE SURCHARGE FEES FROM HUNTERS, ANGLERS, TRAPPERS AND GUIDE OUTFITTERS, and from 2026 the stated priorities are lands providing PUBLIC ACCESS for fishing, hunting and non-motorised recreation, wetland or grassland conservation, and large properties with values such as ungulate winter range. A no-access habitat purchase is a weak fit here; frame the access case honestly or look elsewhere. Proposals are scored on species richness, connectivity, planning priority and IMPENDING THREATS — that last criterion is where a live development proposal counts in your favour. Applications only through their Survey Apply system; email is refused.

trackers.name: HCTF — all grant programmes, amounts and deadlines (BC)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Habitat Conservation Trust Foundation (est. 1981, trustee of the Habitat Conservation Trust under the BC Wildlife Act) runs a ladder of grants, and the smaller rungs are the ones a new group can actually reach. COMMUNITY GRANTS up to $10k for volunteer-driven hands-on work, deadline February. SEED GRANTS up to $10k for proposal development, scoping and technical work — that is money to BUILD a bigger application, deadline November. CAPACITY GRANTS for early-stage planning and skills. LAND STEWARDSHIP GRANTS $10k–$60k for managing NGO-held conservation properties, but note the cycle is EVERY THREE YEARS, so missing it costs you three. WHO IT SUITS: provincial and municipal governments, First Nations, academic institutions, NGOs, industry and community groups. HOW IT DIFFERS: the Seed Grant route means you do not need a finished proposal to start — get funded to write the real one.

trackers.name: Canadian Environmental Law Association (CELA) — Ontario legal aid clinic
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a specialty legal aid clinic funded by Legal Aid Ontario (est. 1970) that will ACT AT HEARINGS AND IN COURT on behalf of citizens or citizens' groups, with nearly 50 years of groundbreaking cases. WHO IT SUITS: Ontario residents and groups for whom cost is the barrier — representation is free for those who qualify on means.

trackers.name: Ontario Land Trust Alliance — find a land trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a registered charity representing the network of land trusts across Ontario, with a searchable directory of members — community-based non-profits that protect natural landscapes, agricultural land and cultural heritage features. More than 85,000 acres protected through Ontario land trusts to date. USE IT: start with the directory to find the trust covering your area rather than approaching a national body. Note the Associate category takes in CONSERVATION AUTHORITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES as well as charities, so the directory can also tell you which public bodies in your area already hold a conservation mandate — useful when you need a local institution to take on a site.

trackers.name: Conservation Ontario — the 36 watershed Conservation Authorities
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the network of Ontario's 36 CONSERVATION AUTHORITIES — local watershed management agencies formed jointly by the province and municipalities under the Conservation Authorities Act 1946, mandated to conserve, restore and manage water, land and natural habitat on a watershed basis. USE IT: unlike a land trust, an authority is a public body with a statutory footing that CONTRIBUTES TO MUNICIPAL PLANNING PROCESSES — so where a development affects floodplain, wetland or watercourse, the relevant authority is a formal participant in the decision, not an outside objector. Find the authority for your watershed and check its position before framing your own. TIMING CAUTION: a provincial proposal to consolidate authority boundaries regionally is live, so confirm which body currently covers your area rather than relying on an older map.

trackers.name: Southern Alberta Land Trust Society (SALTS)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a rancher-led, landowner-driven land trust holding CONSERVATION EASEMENTS across Alberta's Eastern Slopes, prairie and foothills — roughly Red Deer south to the US border, the South Saskatchewan River Basin. It accepts donated easements and issues charitable tax receipts (cash, gift and split receipts), and in extraordinary circumstances may consider PURCHASING an easement. USE IT: its stated purpose is supporting landowners who want to keep remaining grassland in grazing rather than see it converted to uses that permanently undermine its benefits — so for Alberta grassland threatened with conversion, this is a direct fit. Be aware they apply an assessment guide and there are grounds on which they will decline an easement; strong landowner representation on the board means the rancher's position carries weight.

trackers.name: The Conservation Trust (Manitoba) — provincial endowment funding
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Manitoba fund delivered by Manitoba Habitat Conservancy and supported by the Province, drawn from a $204 million provincial endowment that also created the GROW and Wetland GROW Trusts. Since 2019 it has invested close to $1.5 million into conservation projects with the Nature Conservancy of Canada alone. Funding categories cover Habitat and Wildlife, Innovation, Conservation Planning, and Connecting People with Nature. WHO IT SUITS: Manitoba habitat, wildlife, water and soil conservation work. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment-backed, so it is not dependent on annual budget rounds the way most government programmes are. NOTE: described here via NCC's own site; Manitoba Habitat Conservancy's own domain not verified this session.

trackers.name: Nature Saskatchewan — stewardship, sanctuaries and easement support
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Saskatchewan's provincial nature society (since 1949), holding nature sanctuaries and running the Stewards of Saskatchewan programmes — Operation Burrowing Owl, Shrubs for Shrikes, Plovers on Shore and Rare Plant Rescue — which work with landowners on species-at-risk habitat. READ THIS LIMIT FIRST: by its own statement NATURE SASKATCHEWAN DOES NOT ACTIVELY PURSUE THE HOLDING OF CONSERVATION EASEMENTS. It explains them and will give logistical support to a landowner who wants to establish one, but you will need a different holder — in Saskatchewan an easement can be held by a conservation organisation, a government agency OR A RURAL MUNICIPALITY, which is a route worth remembering where no trust is active. USE IT: the other reason to contact them is evidential — they collect biodiversity information that is used in assessing the environmental impact of land development, so if you need documented species records for a threatened site, this is where they are.

trackers.name: Nova Scotia Nature Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the province's only conservation charity dedicated solely to Nova Scotian land, protecting it either by CONSERVATION AGREEMENT with a private landowner or by ACQUIRING THE LAND ITSELF, in perpetuity — more than 200 sites over 30 years. USE IT: the reason a land trust matters more here than almost anywhere else in Canada is ownership. By the Trust's own account 65% of Nova Scotia and 85% OF ITS COASTLINE ARE PRIVATELY OWNED, against roughly 90% public ownership across the rest of the country. Provincial protected-area designation simply cannot reach most Nova Scotian land, so if a coastal or old-forest site is threatened here, a private conservation agreement or purchase is often the ONLY route — not a fallback.

trackers.name: Nova Scotia Environment — private land conservation
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the province's own page on securing ecologically significant private land, noting that SEVERAL PROVINCIAL STATUTES enable private land protection and that the department works in partnership with the Nova Scotia Nature Trust on conservation projects. USE IT: to identify which provincial statutory instrument fits your parcel before approaching anyone — the route differs by mechanism, and a landowner who already wants to protect their land may qualify for a designation rather than needing a sale.

trackers.name: Nature Trust of New Brunswick
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a provincial land trust (formed 1987) that conserves and stewards PRIVATE land in New Brunswick, holding more than 100 nature preserves including entire islands in the Bay of Fundy. Runs a land stewardship programme with farmers and landowners where the owner commits to conservation measures WITHOUT handing over any control. USE IT: two routes rather than one — outright protection of a parcel, or a stewardship agreement for an owner who wants to keep managing their own land. The Trust also holds land in trust for, and has transferred land to, Indigenous land-conservation groups in the province, so it is a realistic partner where a site has both ecological and territorial significance.

trackers.name: Nature Trust of New Brunswick — land conservation options
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a charitable land trust (est. 1987) that conserves private land in New Brunswick by purchase, donation and conservation easement, now holding around 100 nature preserves — including entire islands in the Bay of Fundy. USE IT: this page is the intake route. They assess EACH PARCEL ON ITS OWN ECOLOGICAL MERITS, so the pitch matters: species at risk found in only a handful of places, wide-ranging species such as Canada lynx, Appalachian hardwood or old Acadian forest, wetlands, rare plant habitat, or areas important for migrating birds and waterfowl breeding. They also run a stewardship programme where a landowner commits to conservation measures WITHOUT handing over any control — the option to raise where an owner is sympathetic but will not sell.

trackers.name: CPAWS Newfoundland & Labrador
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the provincial chapter (founded 2003) of the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society, working specifically to get NEW terrestrial and marine protected areas established in Newfoundland and Labrador and to hold government to managing existing ones properly. Track record includes advancing the South Coast Fjords National Marine Conservation Area and the Eagle River Watershed protected area. USE IT: this is a designation-focused ally rather than a land trust — Newfoundland has no provincial land trust, and protection here runs through the Wilderness and Ecological Reserves Act and the volunteer advisory council (WERAC) that recommends new reserves. CPAWS-NL tracks the 'A Home for Nature' protected areas plan and the public engagement WERAC is running on ten proposed protected areas, so if your site is near one of them there is an open process to push into rather than a cold start.

trackers.name: Nature Conservancy of Canada — Newfoundland and Labrador
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: NCC's provincial programme, conserving ecologically significant land in Newfoundland and Labrador since 1996 by working with private landowners — including large corporate donations of forest land. USE IT: also the route to an unusual provincial mechanism. NCC works with the STEWARDSHIP ASSOCIATION OF MUNICIPALITIES to get natural areas inside municipal boundaries formally recognised as protected areas, via assessment of local land-management practice and stewardship agreements with the provincial government — over 2,600 hectares of municipal public land recognised so far, and the programme is seeking new municipal partners. If the land you are defending is municipally owned, that is a route no land trust offers.

trackers.name: Island Nature Trust (Prince Edward Island)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: PEI's provincial land trust (est. 1979), acquiring ecologically sensitive land by DONATION, BEQUEST OR PURCHASE and managing it to restore ecological integrity — nearly 13,000 acres across more than a hundred Natural Areas. It also assists private landowners to protect their own properties without transferring them. USE IT: 87% OF PEI IS PRIVATELY OWNED, so almost nothing can be protected without a landowner agreeing, and the Trust is built around that. The teeth are statutory: land it takes on is protected from development IN PERPETUITY under the PEI Natural Areas Protection Act, not merely by contract. It also runs a Stewardship Fund so the long-term maintenance cost of a donated property is covered — worth raising with an owner who worries what happens after they hand it over.

trackers.name: CPAWS Northwest Territories
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the NWT chapter of the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society, working from conservation science and in collaboration with communities across the territory on conservation planning and stewardship. USE IT: the NWT is where Indigenous-led protection has gone furthest in Canada — Edéhzíe, established with the Dehcho First Nations, was CANADA'S FIRST INDIGENOUS PROTECTED AND CONSERVED AREA, covering more than 14,000 square kilometres, over twice the size of Banff, managed through a management board and Dehcho Indigenous guardians. Live work includes the Slave River Delta IPCA and the Dehcho Land Use Plan. If you are defending land here, the realistic route runs through Indigenous governments and land use planning rather than acquisition.

trackers.name: CPAWS Yukon
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Whitehorse-based chapter of the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society, working on wilderness protection across the Yukon alongside the territory's 14 First Nations and the Inuvialuit. USE IT: in the Yukon the decisive instrument is LAND USE PLANNING, not land purchase — almost all land is Crown or under settled land claims, so there is no trust to sell to. The precedent to know is the Peel Watershed: in 2017 the SUPREME COURT OF CANADA ruled the Yukon government had to complete meaningful final consultation on a plan protecting 80% of the watershed. CPAWS Yukon tracks the regional planning commissions and pushes for Indigenous Protected and Conserved Areas. The standing risk they flag: mineral development keeps advancing in regions where land use planning has not been completed, so the sequence matters more than the objection.

trackers.name: ANLA + VITAL — national environmental licences
trackers.desc: Colombia's National Environmental Licensing Authority, with VITAL, the single national window where licence files (expedientes) are public. You CAN get: any national-scale project's licence file by name, company or expediente number — the EIA, resolutions, sanctions and modification requests — plus regional authority (CAR) filings routed through the same system. You CAN'T get: full files for some purely municipal permits, and the search interface is exact-match and takes practice. For activists: expediente numbers unlock everything — find the project's LAV/LAM number once and you can track every move the company and the state make, and time interventions to open procedural windows.

trackers.name: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) — Protección de Datos
trackers.desc: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) — Protección de Datos — Colombia’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Procuraduría General de la Nación — Acceso a la Información
trackers.desc: National right-to-information guarantor; Colombia’s Procuraduría (Ministerio Público) acts as garante of the Ley de Transparencia 1712/2014 with disciplinary powers — there is no dedicated information commission, Colombia.

trackers.name: Queremos Datos — FOI requests (COL)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Queremos Datos — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Dejusticia
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Colombian centre for law, justice and society combining research with strategic litigation on rights, including environmental and territorial rights. WHO IT SUITS: Colombian communities where a project threatens collective or territorial rights. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; listed as a participating organisation on aida-americas.org.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Resnatur — Reservas Naturales de la Sociedad Civil
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the association that wrote the Reserva Natural de la Sociedad Civil into articles 109 and 110 of Ley 99 de 1993 — still the only private protected-area category inside Colombia's SINAP — and helps owners set reserves up and register them. Registration with Parques Nacionales enters the reserve in the RUNAP, is recorded against the title at the property registry, and is constitutive of rights: under article 11 of Decreto 1996 de 1999 a registered holder gains the right of prior consent to public investments affecting the reserve. LIMIT: under article 332 of the Constitution and article 7 of Ley 685 de 2001 the subsoil and its minerals belong to the State, so registration does not stop a mining or hydrocarbon title being granted underneath. USE IT: to get a threatened parcel registered, and to gain a consent right over state projects on the surface.

trackers.name: Fundepúblico — Fundación para la Defensa del Interés Público
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Colombian public-interest foundation, one of the five environmental law groups that founded AIDA in 1998, working the acción popular and acción de tutela routes that let any citizen defend collective rights to a healthy environment without showing personal injury. WHO IT SUITS: communities and citizens bringing collective-rights actions. DISCLOSE: it also works with the private sector on compensation and habitat-banking instruments, so it is a mixed practice — it is not known to act for proponents against communities, but ask directly about conflicts before you brief it on a live dispute. Its website is also visibly unmaintained, with template markup rendering on the page, so confirm the team is active by phone first.

trackers.name: Fondo Acción — Fondo para la Acción Ambiental y la Niñez
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: administrator of the TFCA Colombia debt-for-nature agreement signed with the United States in 2004, and of the Fondo de Resiliencia para Niñas, Niños y Mujeres, running repeated open convocatorias with published, unusually explicit eligibility rules. WHO IT SUITS: non-profit organisations with legal representation — and the eligible list names Juntas de Acción Comunal, cabildos indígenas and consejos comunitarios alongside NGOs, so an ethnic-territorial authority can apply in its own name. Typical bar is one to two years of legal existence and six months of relevant experience; some windows are open to individuals. Calls are often restricted to named departments, so check the geography first. HOW IT DIFFERS: it publishes the full bases and the list of selected projects, so you can see who actually got funded before you spend a week writing.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is OPIAC, Organización Nacional de los Pueblos Indígenas de la Amazonía Colombiana — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to OPIAC first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Dejusticia
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Colombian centre for law, justice and society combining research with strategic litigation on rights, including environmental and territorial rights. WHO IT SUITS: Colombian communities where a project threatens collective or territorial rights. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; listed as a participating organisation on aida-americas.org.

trackers.name: Consejo de Redacción
trackers.desc: Colombian investigative network promoting reporting on corruption and public resources.

trackers.name: Colombia Confecamaras (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Colombia Confecamaras (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Colombia — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Colombia
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Colombia — supreme court (Colombia).

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Justice of Colombia
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Justice of Colombia — supreme court (Colombia).

trackers.name: Bogotá
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Colombia) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: SECOP (Colombia Compra Eficiente)
trackers.desc: Colombia's electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Colombia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Corte Constitucional
trackers.desc: Official jurisprudence of Colombia's Constitutional Court. · Find here: the case-law (relatoría) of Colombia's Constitutional Court.

trackers.name: DANE
trackers.desc: Colombia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Colombia.

trackers.name: Función Pública (DAFP)
trackers.desc: Colombia's public-administration department — the Manual del Estado directory of executive entities and the SIGEP asset-and-income declarations of senior officials. — Holds to account: executive entities and senior officials — find the Manual del Estado directory and the SIGEP asset-and-income declarations.

trackers.name: RUES
trackers.desc: Colombia's unified business registry across chambers of commerce. — Holds to account: companies in Colombia — find the unified registry across chambers of commerce of entities and registration data.

trackers.name: Archipelago of San Andrés, Providencia and Santa Catalina
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Colombia) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: CRIC — Consejo Regional Indígena del Cauca
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the association of indigenous authorities to which roughly 90% of Cauca's cabildos belong — 115 cabildos and 11 cabildo associations of the Nasa, Misak, Totoró, Polindara, Guanaco, Kokonuko, Kisgó, Yanacona, Inga and Eperara peoples, across nine zones. Founded in Toribío in 1971, its Plataforma de Lucha has always led with recovering resguardo land and expanding resguardos, and it added defence of the natural and environmental resources of indigenous territories to that list. It runs the Guardia Indígena, the community's own unarmed territorial control body, trained in human rights, self-protection, first response, indigenous jurisdiction and evidence handling. USE IT: if you are a Cauca community, this is your own authority structure for recovering or expanding a resguardo and for physically holding territory. It acts through cabildos, not individuals, and its members are killed for this work.

trackers.name: Movimiento Ríos Vivos
trackers.desc: A movement of fifteen associations and families from the Occidente, Norte and Bajo Cauca sub-regions of Antioquia, formed by people displaced and harmed by the Hidroituango dam on the río Cauca — Colombia's largest, with a 79 km reservoir and a 225 m wall. It is not an NGO acting for affected people; it IS the affected people, organised. Working with partner lawyers it has won two rulings in Bogotá: precautionary measures for Hidroituango victims from the 75th criminal court, and an order for restoration of fundamental rights and reparation from the 45th civil circuit court. It also took a complaint to the Inter-American Development Bank's accountability mechanism. WHO IT SUITS: dam- and mining-affected communities on the Cauca. Note the affected municipalities extend beyond Antioquia into Sucre, Bolívar and Córdoba. Its members face sustained threats and killings.

trackers.name: Fundación Horizonte Verde (Orinoquía)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: based in Cumaral, Meta, a founding member of Resnatur which ran its Nodo Orinoquía for ten years and set up the region's first private reserves in Meta from 1994. It does the technical justification and registration paperwork that turns a working finca into a Reserva Natural de la Sociedad Civil, and publishes free manuals and management plans for reserve owners in the Orinoquía. USE IT: in Meta, Casanare, Arauca or Vichada, to get land registered as an RNSC — more than 200 private reserves covering over 200,000 hectares now exist in the region, in a territory where state protected areas are scarce.

trackers.name: Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública (AAIP)
trackers.desc: Argentina's national authority guaranteeing the right of access to public information and data protection. — Holds to account: Argentine public bodies — find the agency's resolutions guaranteeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Ministerio de la Defensa Pública del Chubut
trackers.desc: Public-defense ministry within the judiciary of Chubut, representing people who cannot afford a lawyer and protecting vulnerable groups — indigenous peoples, people deprived of liberty, victims of police abuse, women and children.

trackers.name: ADC (Asociación por los Derechos Civiles)
trackers.desc: Argentine civil-society organisation (since 1995) and member of the Latin American Legislative Transparency Network. Monitors institutions, proposes political and institutional reforms, and advocates on access to public information and legislative transparency.

trackers.name: ACIJ (Asociación Civil por la Igualdad y la Justicia)
trackers.desc: Argentine civil-rights organisation working on access to public information and legislative transparency.

trackers.name: FARN — Fundación Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Argentina's leading environmental-legal organisation (founded 1985, two years after democracy was restored). Provides FREE legal advice to people of limited means affected by environmental problems, and litigates on behalf of individuals and communities — including Indigenous communities resisting lithium mining, on consulta previa and free, prior and informed consent, access rights and environmental impact assessment. WHO IT SUITS: they prioritise public-interest cases that can set or strengthen jurisprudence, so a case with wider precedent value has the best chance; low-income claimants are explicitly the target of the free advice service.

trackers.name: Fundación Vida Silvestre Argentina
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: one of the few Argentine organisations that actually buys land for conservation. For the Urugua-í reserve in Misiones it identified the property, secured donated funds from three organisations including The Nature Conservancy, and bought 3,243 hectares of Atlantic Forest; the reserve is now managed by the foundation and it holds others across the country. Its earlier work documenting the vulnerability of the Urugua-í basin is what pushed the province to create the 84,000-hectare provincial park in the first place. USE IT: to propose a threatened property for purchase, and for the technical case that moves a provincial government to declare a park around it.

trackers.name: Banco de Bosques
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a foundation that intervenes in the land market itself — it watches classified listings for native forest advertised as apto desarrollo, meaning it already carries a clearance permit, and raises the purchase price through georeferenced donations, where satellite imagery ties each donor to the specific square metres they saved. Bought land is then donated on to expand protected areas: 5,005 hectares of Andean-Patagonian forest annexed to Parque Nacional Los Glaciares, and three chacras of Selva Misionera annexed to Parque Provincial Urugua-í. Its statute commits the forests to protection in perpetuity. WHO IT SUITS: this works the other way round from a grant — if you know of a threatened native forest parcel on the market, especially on the agricultural frontier in Chaco, Jujuy, Formosa or northern Santa Fe, bringing it to them is the ask. HOW IT DIFFERS: it buys the land rather than funding the campaign against clearing it.

trackers.name: Auditoría General de la Nación
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Argentina, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: SAIJ
trackers.desc: Sistema Argentino de Información Jurídica: free case law and legislation. · Find here: Argentina's official legal-information system — legislation, case-law and doctrine (SAIJ).

trackers.name: COMPR.AR
trackers.desc: Argentina's national electronic procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Argentina, and for how much.

trackers.name: Justicia Abierta – Datos Abiertos
trackers.desc: Argentina's open judicial-data portal publishing datasets from the Ministry of Justice and 50+ justice institutions. · Find here: Argentina's open-justice data portal (Justicia Abierta).

trackers.name: Auditoría General de la Nación (AGN)
trackers.desc: Argentina's national external-audit body — control of the national public sector's finances and management. — Holds to account: the national public sector — find external audit reports on how federal funds, programmes and state companies were managed.

trackers.name: Registro de Audiencias de Gestión de Intereses
trackers.desc: National lobbying / interest-meeting register. — Holds to account: those seeking to influence officials — find the register of interest-management meetings with public officials.

trackers.name: Inspección General de Justicia (IGJ)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in the City of Buenos Aires — find the Inspección General de Justicia register of entities and directors.

trackers.name: CSJN – Fallos
trackers.desc: Official rulings of Argentina's Supreme Court of Justice. · Find here: the rulings (Fallos) of Argentina's Supreme Court of Justice.

trackers.name: INDEC
trackers.desc: Argentina's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Argentina.

trackers.name: OIKOS Red Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Mendoza NGO that litigates provincial environmental cases and wins them. Its collective amparo of January 2003 over oil drilling inside the Laguna Llancanelo protected wetland was upheld by the Suprema Corte de Justicia de Mendoza, keeping the hydrocarbon prohibition in place — a rare precedent of a court halting a transnational's plans in a protected area. It also brought the unconstitutionality challenge to Decreto 248/2018 on environmental impact assessment for fracking, drawing amicus briefs from FARN, Earthjustice and AIDA, and in 2025 an amparo over the public hearing for the San Jorge mine at Uspallata. WHO IT SUITS: Mendoza residents and groups facing hydrocarbon, fracking or mining projects, and anyone refused environmental information — access to information is its standing theme. NOTE: the live domain is oikosredambiental.org, not the .org.ar that directories list.

trackers.name: OPSur — Observatorio Petrolero Sur
trackers.desc: Formed in 2008 and working from Neuquén and Río Negro alongside the communities living inside Vaca Muerta, the fracking formation spanning Neuquén, Río Negro, La Pampa and Mendoza. Its strength is documentary: it obtained and analysed 1,184 pages of state inspection records of Comarsa's fracking-waste plants covering 2013 to 2021, showing that provincial, national and municipal authorities knew what was happening and did not act. It took the Vaca Muerta case to the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights with CIEL and the Global Initiative for ESCR, for the Mapuche community of Campo Maripe whose territory was conceded to YPF and Chevron without consultation. WHO IT SUITS: residents and Mapuche lof facing wells, waste plants or pipelines — it supplies evidence and analysis of impact studies, not legal representation.

trackers.name: Ley del Lobby / InfoLobby
trackers.desc: Chile's official lobbying platform recording lobbyist meetings, trips and gifts with public officials. Notably, its scope extends to lobbying of the judicial branch — one of the few regimes worldwide that does so. — Holds to account: anyone lobbying Chilean officials — find logged lobbyist meetings, trips and gifts — uniquely also covering the executive.

trackers.name: Consejo para la Transparencia (CPLT)
trackers.desc: Chile's independent Transparency Council, created by Ley 20.285, and the body you go to when a public agency will not hand over a file. You CAN get: a free amparo — no cost, no lawyer needed — if a request goes unanswered past 20 working days, is refused, comes back incomplete, or arrives late. The deadline is 15 working days from notification of the denial, and the Council can ORDER the agency to release the information; it has done so against ministries and Gendarmería. Its decisions are searchable at jurisprudencia.cplt.cl, so you can check whether a similar refusal has already been overturned. You CAN'T get: speed — an amparo can take up to 120 calendar days — and the agency may then take the decision to the Corte de Apelaciones by reclamo de ilegalidad, delaying release further. For activists: this is the route when an environmental impact file, an inspection record or monitoring data is withheld. The agency cannot refuse because of WHO you are; discrimination is barred by article 11(g). WHEN NOT TO USE IT: the amparo lies against a denial, so you must have filed the underlying request first.

trackers.name: SEA — e-SEIA project evaluation system
trackers.desc: Chile's Environmental Evaluation Service and its e-SEIA platform: every project entering environmental evaluation (DIA or EIA), its full file, and the citizen-participation (PAC) and indigenous-consultation (PCPI) processes. You CAN get: the complete study and evaluation file for any project by name or region, the RCA resolutions that approve or reject, and formal PAC windows where anyone can file observations (and demand PAC even on DIAs). You CAN'T get: projects that never entered the system. For activists: an unfavourable RCA legally blocks execution — the observation record you build in PAC is also the foundation for reclamation before the environmental tribunals.

trackers.name: FIMA (Fiscalía del Medio Ambiente)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Chile's public-interest environmental law NGO — despite the name it is a non-governmental organisation, not a public prosecutor. Works on environmental litigation and access to environmental justice. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing projects going through Chile's SEIA environmental assessment system. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; listed as a participating organisation on aida-americas.org.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Fundación Tierra Austral — Derecho Real de Conservación
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Chile's first land trust, founded 2012, and co-author of Ley 20.930 (2016) creating the Derecho Real de Conservación — a new real property right letting an owner bind their land to conservation in perpetuity while keeping title. The law requires the holding counterparty to be a non-profit without conflicting interests; Tierra Austral acts as that holder. USE IT: to lock a Chilean property against development permanently and against any future owner, without the state buying or declaring it.

trackers.name: Defensoría Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Chilean association, interdisciplinary and mainly women-led, giving legal representation plus communications and technical support to communities in environmental conflicts — it sued the state and the companies operating in the Quintero-Puchuncaví sacrifice zone over accumulated environmental damage, and has taken community representatives to the UN Universal Periodic Review. WHO IT SUITS: organised communities and territorial and indigenous organisations, not individuals. Its founding premise is that the cost of environmental defence should be collective rather than borne by the affected community, so it fundraises to cover the lawyers and the expert reports that ordinary judicial assistance in Chile will not fund.

trackers.name: ONG FIMA — Fiscalía del Medio Ambiente
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Chile's first and largest public-interest environmental law office, a non-profit founded in 1998 and explicitly independent of any government body or party — which is what lets it take cases against the state. Its record includes the Mina Invierno blasting case on Isla Riesco, ended when the Supreme Court rejected the last cassation appeals. WHO IT SUITS: communities and citizens facing a project or environmental damage. Its Poder Ambiental platform gives FREE remote legal orientation — plain-language guides to citizen complaints and the environmental institutions, a forum, and a route to FIMA lawyers — built deliberately around the many steps that need no lawyer at all.

trackers.name: Fondo Naturaleza Chile
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Chile's national environmental fund, created to mobilise and complement the finance needed for conservation and restoration in a country that is both exceptionally biodiverse and among the most exposed to climate impacts and biodiversity loss in the region. It is part of the RedLAC network of Latin American and Caribbean environmental funds. WHO IT SUITS: check its current instruments before assuming — as a national fund it works largely through programmes and partnerships rather than a standing open call, so the realistic route is often a co-financing conversation rather than a grant application. HOW IT DIFFERS: it is the country-level counterpart to the regional funds, and the only Chilean body of its kind.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Chile, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: datos.gob.cl
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Chile.

trackers.name: Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas (INE)
trackers.desc: Chile's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Chile.

trackers.name: InfoProbidad
trackers.desc: National — public portal of officials’ declarations of interests and assets (Contraloría / CPLT).

trackers.name: Mercado Público (ChileCompra)
trackers.desc: Chile's public-procurement marketplace — every state tender and purchase order. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Chile, and for how much.

trackers.name: Poder Judicial de Chile
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal: judgments, case search and court statistics. · Find here: the Chilean Judiciary's portal with case search and judgments.

trackers.name: Registro de Empresas y Sociedades
trackers.desc: Chile's online company and partnership register. — Holds to account: companies in Chile — find the online company-and-partnership register of entities and constitution data.

trackers.name: MapBiomas Alerta — validated deforestation reports
trackers.desc: A multi-institution Brazilian network that validates every deforestation alert with high-resolution satellite imagery and publishes a ready-to-use report per event — before/after images, area, overlap with the CAR rural registry, protected areas and settlements. You CAN get: court-grade documentation of specific deforestation events anywhere in Brazil, free, weekly. You CAN'T get: the perpetrator's name directly — but the CAR overlap usually identifies the property holder. For activists: this is the 'photo of the licence plate' — when land is being cleared near your territory, the Alerta report is evidence you can hand to IBAMA, the Ministério Público or the press the same week it happens.

trackers.name: Fiquem Sabendo
trackers.desc: Brazilian nonprofit specialising in freedom-of-information requests and public-data access to expose government. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find FOI requests, public datasets and access casework.

trackers.name: Acesso à Informação (Brasil)
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal access-to-information service under the LAI — request portal and transparency monitoring. — Holds to account: Brazilian federal bodies — find how to file LAI requests, response statistics and transparency monitoring.

trackers.name: CGU – Lei de Acesso à Informação
trackers.desc: Federal comptroller administering Brazil's Access to Information Law (LAI) and transparency portals. · Find here: Brazil's Comptroller-General — access-to-information oversight under the Lei de Acesso à Informação.

trackers.name: DataJud (Base Nacional)
trackers.desc: CNJ's National Judicial Database centralising case metadata and statistics from every Brazilian court, with a public API. · Find here: the CNJ's national caseload database (DataJud) behind the 'Justiça em Números' statistics.

trackers.name: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Brazilian civil association (OSCIP, founded 1994) working alongside Indigenous, quilombola and extractivist communities on territorial defence, rights and protection of their lands, with permanent offices in São Paulo, Brasília, Manaus, Boa Vista, São Gabriel da Cachoeira, Canarana, Eldorado and Altamira. Intervenes across the executive, legislative and judicial branches, and runs the De Olho no Xingu observatory, which monitors public administrative processes for infrastructure and mining works and feeds the Rede Xingu+ Radar de Obras. WHO IT SUITS: Indigenous, quilombola and traditional communities in Brazil facing large works, mining or land-grabbing — especially in the Amazon, the Xingu, Rio Negro and Vale do Ribeira.

trackers.name: Funbio — Fundo Brasileiro para a Biodiversidade
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Brazil's biodiversity fund, active since 1996, running all its calls through one public portal at chamadas.funbio.org.br — Floresta Viva restoration editais with BNDES, territorial programmes such as Biodiversidade do Litoral do Paraná, and the Fundo Kayapó. WHO IT SUITS: non-profits — associações civis, private foundations, cooperatives — usually needing two years of legal existence; some windows go further, the Kayapó calls requiring a wholly Kayapó council. HOW IT DIFFERS: much of the money is compensation attached to a defined territory, so eligibility is often geographic before it is thematic — read the municipality list first.

trackers.name: Terra de Direitos
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a human-rights organisation founded in Curitiba in 2002 working through assessoria jurídica popular — legal advice built with the movement rather than delivered to it — in collective conflicts over rural and urban land, quilombola titling, indigenous territory, seeds and biodiversity, with offices in Curitiba, Santarém and Brasília. It pairs strategic litigation with monitoring of megaprojects and defence of threatened land defenders. WHO IT SUITS: collective claimants — social movements, quilombola associations, traditional communities — in partnership with organised movements, not individual clients. Strongest in Paraná, the Cerrado and the Lower Amazon around Santarém.

trackers.name: SOS Mata Atlântica — SAD, alertas de desmatamento
trackers.desc: A Brazilian foundation running since 1986, whose most directly usable output is the SAD Mata Atlântica alert system. You CAN get: monthly deforestation alerts from high-resolution Sentinel imagery, published through MapBiomas Alerta and in quarterly bulletins, each carrying a technical laudo saying whether the clearing was for agriculture, urban expansion or mining — and linking it to a CAR rural land registration where one exists, which names the property. You CAN'T get: coverage outside the Atlantic Forest biome, or enforcement — the system feeds IBAMA, state environmental secretariats and police, and the state Ministérios Públicos. For activists: this is how you reach a prosecutor with a dated, geolocated, property-linked clearing already documented.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is COIAB, Coordenação das Organizações Indígenas da Amazônia Brasileira — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to COIAB first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Brazilian Election Justice
trackers.desc: Brazilian Election Justice — tribunal (Brazil).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Brazil, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado da Bahia
trackers.desc: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado da Bahia — appellate court (Brazil).

trackers.name: Agência Pública
trackers.desc: Brazil's pioneering nonprofit investigative-journalism agency, reporting on public money, land, corruption and abuses of power.

trackers.name: dados.gov.br
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: INESC (Institute of Socioeconomic Studies)
trackers.desc: Brazilian non-profit (est. 1979) analysing the federal public budget through a human-rights and equity lens and advocating fiscal transparency. Here you can trace how Brazil's federal budget allocates money, analysed through a human-rights and equity lens.

trackers.name: STF – Jurisprudência
trackers.desc: Official jurisprudence search of the Supremo Tribunal Federal. · Find here: the case-law (jurisprudência) of Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU)
trackers.desc: Federal Court of Accounts auditing public spending. Here you can trace public-audit findings on waste, irregularity and misspending in Brazil.

trackers.name: Portal da Transparência (Brasil)
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal transparency portal: detailed spending, suppliers, contracts, tax expenditures and open data/APIs. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: Portal da Transparência
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal transparency portal of revenues, spending and transfers. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: Central das Emendas
trackers.desc: Independent Brazilian organisation dedicated to transparency of parliamentary budget amendments (emendas parlamentares), with a searchable tool for the low-oversight 'Emendas PIX' (special transfers), data panels and research.

trackers.name: Financial Activities Control Board
trackers.desc: the national Financial Intelligence Unit of Brazil linked to the Central Bank of Brazil

trackers.name: Federal District
trackers.desc: Sub-national government portal (Brazil) — entry point to this unit's budget, procurement and finance information.

trackers.name: Defensoria Pública da União (Federal Public Defender) of Brazil
trackers.desc: National institution of Brazil that provides free legal representation and defends access to justice, fair-trial and due-process rights for people who cannot afford counsel.

trackers.name: Compras.gov.br
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal procurement portal (formerly ComprasNet) for tenders and contracts. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Brazil, and for how much.

trackers.name: Empresas – gov.br (Juntas Comerciais)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Brazil — find access to the state commercial-registry (Juntas Comerciais) network of entities and filings.

trackers.name: National Register of Legal Persons (CNPJ)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Brazilian Institute of Geography & Statistics (IBGE)
trackers.desc: Brazil's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Brazil.

trackers.name: Jusbrasil
trackers.desc: Brazil's largest structured legal database — jurisprudence, case tracking and doctrine across all courts. · Find here: a large aggregator of Brazilian case-law, legislation and legal news (JusBrasil; some content gated).

trackers.name: JusBrasil
trackers.desc: Large aggregator of Brazilian case law and legal documents. · Find here: a large aggregator of Brazilian case-law, legislation and legal news (JusBrasil; some content gated).

trackers.name: Observatório Social do Brasil (Sistema OSB)
trackers.desc: National non-profit network (since 2008) coordinating 70+ local Social Observatories across 100+ municipalities. Volunteers monitor municipal public spending, procurement (licitações) and contracts in real time, publishing findings and a Public Transparency & Governance Index of city and state governments.

trackers.name: Instituto Guaicuy — Assessoria Técnica Independente
trackers.desc: The lever to know in Minas Gerais: since early 2021 an Assessoria Técnica Independente is a RIGHT of dam-affected people under the state Política Estadual de Pessoas Atingidas por Barragens, and the adviser is chosen democratically by the affected communities themselves, not by the company. Guaicuy serves in that role for communities hit by the 2019 Vale dam collapse across Pompéu, Curvelo, Felixlândia, Três Marias, São Gonçalo do Abaeté, Martinho Campos, Morada Nova de Minas, Biquinhas, Paineiras and Abaeté, and for the Doutor dam decommissioning at Antônio Pereira, Ouro Preto. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing a mining company across a table with far better technical and legal resources — the ATI exists precisely to close that asymmetry, covering damage assessment, compensation matrices and monitoring of the reparation agreement.

trackers.name: NACAB — Núcleo de Assessoria às Comunidades Atingidas por Barragens
trackers.desc: A second Independent Technical Assistance body operating in Minas Gerais, working with communities affected by the Brumadinho collapse and, under licensing Condicionante 39, with thirteen communities across Alvorada de Minas, Dom Joaquim and Conceição do Mato Dentro. That condicionante is the point worth knowing: a mining licence can itself require the company to fund an independent adviser that the affected communities choose. WHO IT SUITS: dam- and mine-affected communities entering a reparation process — NACAB does the loss-and-damage survey, the valuation of what should be indemnified, and monitors delivery of what was agreed. Choose between the accredited ATIs rather than approaching one at random; the selection is run by the public prosecutors and defensoría.

trackers.name: SPVS (Paraná) — RPPNs e reservas próprias
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Curitiba conservation organisation founded in 1984, an OSCIP since 2001, which owns and manages 19,000 hectares of its own reserves on the northern Paraná coast — Águas and Guaricica in Antonina, Papagaio-de-Cara-Roxa in Guaraqueçaba — and works with private owners to turn land into RPPNs, the only private protected-area category in the national SNUC system. USE IT: to get Atlantic Forest land in Paraná protected as an RPPN or acquired outright. The argument that lands with owners and mayors: Paraná's ICMS Ecológico redistributes a share of state tax to municipalities holding conservation units, so an RPPN pays the municipality real money every year — Antonina and Guaraqueçaba have drawn millions of reais on the back of SPVS reserves alone.

trackers.name: RPPNM Curitiba — Secretaria Municipal do Meio Ambiente
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Curitiba's municipal environment secretariat runs the Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural Municipal, the city-level private reserve Brazil's first municipality created for URBAN green land. You apply to the SMMA through the PROCEC electronic portal with a management and conservation plan; if approved the reserve is created by municipal decree, in perpetuity and irrevocably, recorded against your title at the property register. Live and current — reserves were still being created by decree in 2026. USE IT: the incentives are the point, and they are financial. Full exemption from IPTU urban property tax on the wooded land, and transfer of 100% of the building rights you give up to unrestricted parts of the city — which you may sell on the construction market. Land stays yours; the reserve may be used for visitation, ecotourism, education and research. For an owner of a wooded urban lot under development pressure, this converts the threat into an asset.

trackers.name: Idesam — Instituto de Conservação e Desenvolvimento Sustentável da Amazônia
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Manaus-based institute working across the interior of Amazonas state, whose concrete offer to a community is technical assistance to get a Plano de Manejo Florestal written, certified and selling. Through the Cidades Florestais project, backed by the Fundo Amazônia and BNDES, it works with residents, settlers and extractivists in fourteen Amazonas municipalities; the Uatumã reserve association it supported won FSC certification and saw its oil price rise from R$1 to R$8 a kilo, with average income for 370 extractivists reaching close to R$3,000. USE IT: where community forest management is the realistic alternative to illegal logging on your territory, and you need the plan, the equipment and the buyer, not a lawyer.

trackers.name: Movimento Xingu Vivo Para Sempre
trackers.desc: Based in Altamira and formed in 2008 at the second Encontro dos Povos do Xingu, which brought together more than two thousand indigenous people, ribeirinhos, small farmers and fishers against Belo Monte. It is the movement of the affected themselves, working with territorial organisations, traditional communities, fishers, women's movements and periphery residents, and it has supported legal actions nationally and internationally alongside partner NGOs and the Federal Public Prosecutors' Office. It is now the main opposition to Belo Sun, which would be Brazil's largest open-pit gold mine with a tailings dam nearly three times the size of Brumadinho's. WHO IT SUITS: communities of the Middle Xingu and Volta Grande facing the dam's aftermath or the mine — including on where Belo Monte's royalties actually go, which it campaigns to put under community oversight.

trackers.name: SEMARNAT Gaceta Ecológica + SINAT
trackers.desc: Mexico's weekly federal gazette of every project entering environmental impact evaluation (PEIA), with the SINAT system holding the underlying files. You CAN get: which projects entered evaluation this week and where, the MIA (impact statement) itself, resolutions approving or rejecting, and the legal trigger for demanding a consulta pública — you have 10 days from Gaceta publication to request one. You CAN'T get: state-level projects evaluated by state authorities. For activists: this is the early-warning system — read the Gaceta for your state weekly, and the 10-day consulta clock plus the MIA's own weaknesses are the two levers Mexican communities have used to stop everything from marinas to mines.

trackers.name: Centro Prodh (Miguel Agustín Pro Juárez)
trackers.desc: Jesuit-founded Mexican human-rights organization (est. 1988) based in Mexico City — defends victims of arbitrary detention, torture, enforced disappearance and extrajudicial execution through a multidisciplinary “integral defense” methodology combining strategic litigation, psychological and social accompaniment and advocacy; it has taken emblematic cases (including Ayotzinapa, Atenco and Tlatlaya) to the Inter-American Court and generated jurisprudence on due process, torture and the rights of indigenous prisoners.

trackers.name: Centro de Derechos Humanos Fray Bartolomé de Las Casas (FrayBa)
trackers.desc: The Centro de Derechos Humanos Fray Bartolmé de las Casa is a non-profit organisation that works to defend and promote the human rights of Indigenous peoples in the state of Chiapas, Mexico, through the promotion of peaceful and civil proposals.

trackers.name: Transparencia para el Pueblo
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; Transparencia para el Pueblo is the federal access-to-information body created in 2025 — a deconcentrated unit under the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno that absorbed most functions of the abolished autonomous INAI, handling federal transparency appeals and the National Transparency Platform, Mexico.

trackers.name: Fondo Acción Solidaria (FASOL)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Mexico-based grantmaker and Global Greengrants partner making small grants on an integrated social-and-environmental approach, decided close to the ground. WHO IT SUITS: Mexican community groups needing modest, fast funding without an international application cycle. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as a grantmaking partner on greengrants.org.

trackers.name: CEMDA — Centro Mexicano de Derecho Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Mexico's principal environmental-law organisation and a founding member of AIDA. Litigates environmental cases and supports communities against harmful projects. WHO IT SUITS: Mexican communities challenging permits or impact assessments. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as an AIDA founder on aida-americas.org.

trackers.name: MAR Fund — Small Grants Program (Mesoamerican Reef)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an ecoregional fund created in 2004 by the national conservation funds of Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, running a Small Grants Program by competitive Call for Proposals — now past its 17th call — with two windows, the Traditional Window and the Reef Rescue Initiative. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. HOW IT DIFFERS: transnational by design, so a project spanning the reef across two countries is a fit here where a national funder would balk.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Fondo Mexicano para la Conservación de la Naturaleza (FMCN)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Mexico's national environmental fund since 1994, channelling endowment income and international money through periodic convocatorias — open calls for non-reimbursable grants, including Fomafur (fire management and restoration) and Conserva Aves. WHO IT SUITS: legally constituted local civil-society organisations — FMCN's own term is Organizaciones Locales Legalmente Constituidas — not individuals or unincorporated collectives. HOW IT DIFFERS: an endowed fund, not a campaign donor; frame the ask as long-term protection and management of a defined area.

trackers.name: Pronatura Noroeste — private land-protection instruments
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the northwest arm of Mexico's oldest conservation NGO, working across nine states and reporting 266,000 hectares protected with private legal instruments — outright land purchase and servidumbres ecológicas, the ecological easement under which one owner permanently restricts development on their parcel in favour of another. USE IT: to get a threatened parcel bought or permanently encumbered instead of fought permit by permit, especially coastal wetland and estuary in Baja California, BCS, Sonora and Sinaloa.

trackers.name: FASOL — Fondo Acción Solidaria
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Mexican fund constituted in 2007 that moves flexible money straight to grassroots groups, collectives and communities defending their territory — small seed contributions rather than big project grants, with a capacity-building programme and mentoring network attached. WHO IT SUITS: unincorporated collectives and communities, not only registered A.C.s — this is the door that stays open when the big national funds demand legal personality. It explicitly funds responses to threats against territory and collective rights. HOW IT DIFFERS from FMCN: grassroots-facing philanthropy built to reach groups nobody else will bank. NOTE the canonical domain is fasol-ac.org, not fasol.org.mx.

trackers.name: Centro Mexicano Pro Bono
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a clearinghouse that brokers free legal accompaniment from commercial law firms to communities and civil-society organisations, with a stated environmental-defence line covering constitutional, administrative, environmental and regulatory litigation — amparo proceedings, filings and appeals before authorities, and legal opinions. For a small organisation it can also cover the unglamorous work: reviewing a contract clause, fixing your legal structure, meeting your compliance obligations. WHO IT SUITS: community groups and CSOs with no budget for counsel. DISCLOSE: the lawyers come from commercial firms donating time, so conflicts with a specific company are a real possibility — name the developer you are up against when you first make contact and ask them to run a conflicts check before you share anything.

trackers.name: IDEA — Instituto de Derecho Ambiental A.C.
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a public-interest environmental law office constituted in Guadalajara in 1997, founded expressly because western Mexico had no public-interest environmental lawyers. Its stated work is supporting indigenous communities defending their natural resources and promoting the environmental and territorial rights of communities in situations of vulnerability. Its founders ran the first environmental law workshops in Mexico with the Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide, alongside the newly formed CEMDA. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous and rural communities in the occidente — Jalisco and neighbouring states — where CEMDA and AIDA are Mexico City-centred. NOTE: its canonical domain could not be verified live this session; it is listed by the Mexican Committee of the IUCN at comitemexicanouicn.org, which is the route to reach it.

trackers.desc: Non-partisan Mexican think-tank producing evidence-based public-finance, competitiveness and anti-corruption analysis and policy proposals. Here you can trace Mexico's public-finance, competitiveness and anti-corruption analysis from IMCO.

WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. HOW IT DIFFERS: transnational by design, so a project spanning the reef across two countries is a fit here where a national funder would balk.

trackers.name: Sociedad de Historia Natural Niparajá
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: founded in La Paz in 1990, and one of the few Mexican organisations that buys land outright for conservation — from 2001 it purchased property on the open market to create the Reserva Natural El Portezuelo, now over 7,300 hectares certified with CONANP as an Área Destinada Voluntariamente a la Conservación. Its land programme covers 350,000 hectares of priority terrestrial and coastal habitat, with a stated goal of a million toward a Sierras Giganta y Guadalupe biosphere reserve. It also built Mexico's first network of Zonas de Refugio Pesquero, in the San Cosme–Punta Coyote corridor, with community surveillance backed by CONAPESCA and PROFEPA. USE IT: to get a Baja California Sur property bought or certified as an ADVC, and for the water-quality monitoring it uses to argue the Sierra watershed against open-pit mining.

trackers.name: Cooperativa AMBIO — programa Scolel'te
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a cooperative based in San Cristóbal de las Casas running Scolel'te — Tseltal for 'the tree that grows' — started in 1997 with campesino communities of the Selva Lacandona, ECOSUR and the University of Edinburgh, and the longest-running programme of its kind in the voluntary carbon market anywhere. It pays landholders directly for reforesting and sustainably managing their own land under the Plan Vivo standard, a methodology that originated in Chiapas. WHO IT SUITS: ejidatarios, communities and smallholders in Chiapas who hold their land — over 1,500 participate and more than 2,500 families receive payments through some 100 organised working groups, including Tojolabal, Tsotsil, Tseltal, Lacandón and Chol communities. You need tenure and a working group, not a legal case. HOW IT DIFFERS: recurring payments to the landholder, not a project grant to an NGO.

trackers.name: EDUCA — Servicios para una Educación Alternativa
trackers.desc: Thirty years old and fifteen of them accompanying community defence against mining in Oaxaca, where its own research counts 294 live mining concessions as of 2020, some 5% of the state under concession, and at least 66 projects labelled 'small' hydroelectric — in one case nine on a single river. It accompanied the eleven Valles Centrales communities that took amparos against concessions granted without their consent and won a suspensión de plano. WHO IT SUITS: agrarian and municipal authorities and community assemblies, not individuals — the amparos are brought by the assembly. It convenes through the Colectivo Oaxaqueño en Defensa de los Territorios and REDECOM, the state community defenders network, so it is also the way into a wider bloc.

trackers.name: Pronatura Veracruz
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Veracruz arm of Pronatura, working the windward slope of the Cofre de Perote on cloud-forest protection with Rainforest Trust funding, and building protection around ejido common lands and local owners rather than around them — the areas it protects include the Reserva Ecológica La Cortadura, the Reserva Campesina Parcela 23 and the Reserva Privada de Conservación Ejido Las Carabinas. USE IT: if you hold or share ejido land in Veracruz and want it recognised as a campesino or private conservation reserve, and for help standing up a community patrol brigade to watch it afterwards.

trackers.name: Procuraduría de los Derechos Humanos (PDH)
trackers.desc: Procuraduría de los Derechos Humanos (PDH) — Guatemala’s Human Rights Ombudsman — the authority overseeing the Law on Access to Public Information, monitoring compliance and receiving complaints. — Holds to account: Guatemala’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information compliance reports and complaints handling.

trackers.name: Centro para la Acción Legal en Derechos Humanos (CALDH)
trackers.desc: Guatemalan human-rights legal center — strategic litigation for indigenous peoples and victims of the armed conflict (including the Ixil genocide and enforced-disappearance cases), defense of criminalized human-rights defenders, and Inter-American system casework.

trackers.name: UDEFEGUA — Unidad de Protección a Defensoras y Defensores de Derechos Humanos
trackers.desc: Guatemala’s human-rights-defenders protection organisation, operating since 2000 and independent since 2009. It registers, verifies and accompanies attacks on defenders — including Indigenous authorities, journalists and land and justice activists — provides an integrated protection system and, increasingly, direct legal defence against criminalisation (for example taking on the technical defence of prosecuted journalists), and publishes the country’s emblematic annual report on the situation of defenders. It also supports defenders across Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and southern Mexico.

trackers.name: MAR Fund — Small Grants Program (Mesoamerican Reef)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an ecoregional fund created in 2004 by the national conservation funds of Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, running a Small Grants Program by competitive Call for Proposals — now past its 17th call — with two windows, the Traditional Window and the Reef Rescue Initiative. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. HOW IT DIFFERS: transnational by design, so a project spanning the reef across two countries is a fit here where a national funder would balk.

trackers.name: Fundación Defensores de la Naturaleza
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: in 1990 became the first NGO in Latin America legally entrusted with managing a state protected area; now co-manages four covering about 5% of Guatemala, and separately creates and runs private and municipal reserves, mainly in the dry Motagua valley. USE IT: to get a threatened property declared and managed as a private or municipal reserve, and for a partner with standing inside the protected-areas system.

trackers.name: CALAS — Centro de Acción Legal-Ambiental y Social de Guatemala
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Guatemalan environmental-law organisation that has repeatedly stopped mines in court. It filed the constitutional amparo against the Progreso VII Derivada mining licence at La Puya on the ground that indigenous communities were never consulted as ILO Convention 169 requires, and was the amparo petitioner in the Escobal / San Rafael case — both recorded on the Ministry of Energy and Mines' own case pages, and in both the courts suspended the operation. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous and campesino communities facing a licence granted without consultation, and defenders being criminalised. It works on collective rights rather than individual claims, and it also joins criminal proceedings as a plaintiff where officials or companies have broken the environmental framework. NOTE: its canonical domain could not be verified live this session — reach it through the case records on the Ministry of Energy and Mines site, mem.gob.gt.
