trackers.name: Defensoría del Pueblo del Ecuador
trackers.desc: Defensoría del Pueblo del Ecuador — Ecuador’s Ombudsman — the guarantor body for the Organic Law on Transparency and Access to Public Information (LOTAIP), monitoring compliance and handling complaints. — Holds to account: Ecuador’s public bodies on disclosure — find LOTAIP compliance reports, complaints handling and guidance.

trackers.name: Fundación Regional de Asesoría en Derechos Humanos (INREDH)
trackers.desc: Ecuadorian human-rights foundation (est. 1993) — provides legal assistance and accompaniment to victims of grave rights violations and their families, litigates cases of enforced disappearance, torture and criminalized protest, and defends indigenous-peoples’ and nature rights.

trackers.name: ECOLEX — Corporación de Gestión y Derecho Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Ecuadorian environmental-law NGO founded in 1998 with a standing Litigio Ambiental practice and two tools most groups never hear about — Línea Verde, a free national phone and email line for reporting environmental damage and getting advice on your rights and the rights of nature, and a community paralegal programme that trains a recognised local leader in environmental, agrarian and organisational law inside their own community. WHO IT SUITS: rural, indigenous and peri-urban communities facing damage or a land conflict who need a first legal read at no cost, and groups that want their own trained paralegal rather than a lawyer flown in. The site has not been refreshed since 2016, so confirm current staffing by phone.

trackers.name: Fondo del Biocorredor Amazónico (Fondo BCA)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the vehicle channelling Ecuador's December 2024 debt-for-nature conversion, which refinanced roughly USD 1,530 million of sovereign debt and secured hundreds of millions for conservation. It launched its first grant convocatoria in April 2026, funding conservation, restoration and bioeconomy projects, with targets of 4.6 million hectares of protected areas better managed, 1.8 million hectares of additional forest and wetland protected, 18,000 km of rivers safeguarded and 40,000 hectares restored. WHO IT SUITS: organisations working in the Ecuadorian Amazon. Selection weights technical viability and management of social and environmental risk, so a community proposal will need a technical partner. HOW IT DIFFERS: new money on a fixed programme timetable — the early calls are the accessible ones.

trackers.name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía — Convocatorias (Ecuador)
trackers.desc: Ecuador's national environmental authority, which publishes its open calls on a standing Convocatorias page. You CAN get: grant and selection calls aimed at civil society — recent ones include support for Indigenous peoples' initiatives in the Putumayo-Içá basin under a GEF-financed, World Bank-implemented project, and the executing-entity selection for the Amazon Biocorridor Fund — alongside the ministry's public notices to affected residents about environmental registrations for specific operations. You CAN'T get: any assurance a call is still open; dates pass quickly and the page is not archived. For activists: the same page carries the citizen-notification notices, so it is worth watching for the first public sign that something is being permitted near you.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is CONFENIAE, Confederación de las Nacionalidades Indígenas de la Amazonía Ecuatoriana — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to CONFENIAE first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Senace — EVA environmental certification registry
trackers.desc: Peru's national reviewer of the biggest projects' environmental studies (EIA-d) in mining, energy, hydrocarbons, transport, agriculture and waste, with the EVA single-window where every study is filed. You CAN get: the full EIA, its resolutions, the company and consultant behind a project, its current stage, and a formal channel to submit citizen observations during participación ciudadana. You CAN'T get: projects below the detailed-EIA threshold (those sit with sector ministries or regions). For activists: when a mine or pipeline is announced near your community, pull its EIA here before it's approved — the comment window is your legal opening, and the study's own baseline data becomes your evidence.

trackers.name: OEFA — environmental enforcement + SINADA complaints
trackers.desc: Peru's environmental enforcement agency for mining, energy, fisheries and industry, with public enforcement reporting (PIFA portal) and SINADA, where any citizen can file an environmental complaint. You CAN get: supervision and sanction records against named companies, administrative measures, and a formal complaint channel that obliges a response. You CAN'T get: criminal prosecution (that's the Fiscalía Ambiental) or enforcement in sectors held by regional EFAs. For activists: a contaminated river or illegal discharge becomes actionable the moment it's a SINADA case number — and a company's OEFA sanction history is ammunition in any campaign against its next project.

trackers.name: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (ANTAIP)
trackers.desc: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (ANTAIP) — Peru’s national authority for transparency and access to public information (within the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights). — Holds to account: Peru’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information guidance, supervision and reports.

trackers.name: Manolo (manolo.rocks)
trackers.desc: Civic tool scraping Peru's official visitor/interest-management logs to expose who meets public officials. — Holds to account: those who meet Peruvian officials — find a civic tool scraping official visitor logs to expose who met whom.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Transparencia y Acceso a la Informacion Publica (Peru)
trackers.desc: Peru's Transparency and Access to Information Tribunal, the last administrative instance when a public body refuses a request. You CAN get: a free appeal, filed online through the gob.pe mesa de partes, which the Tribunal must resolve within 10 working days; the Ministry of Justice publishes a model appeal form you can adapt. The deadline is 15 working days from an EXPRESS refusal — but where the body simply stayed silent, a tacit denial, there is NO time limit, so an old unanswered request is still live. The Tribunal applies the exceptions in articles 15 to 17 restrictively: an agency stamping a document reservado without justifying it has no effect. You CAN'T get: enforcement beyond the administrative route. For activists: use it for withheld permit files, inspection reports or concession records. WHEN NOT TO USE IT — the useful part: you do NOT have to exhaust this route. A habeas data action goes straight to a civil judge within 60 working days of the refusal, so if the matter is urgent, go to court instead of appealing here.

trackers.name: Comision de Derechos Humanos (COMISEDH)
trackers.desc: Peru Comision de Derechos Humanos is a non-profit association that is dedicated to the protection and promotion of human rights in Peru. It mainly works on combatting torture and sexual violence against women and girls. It also supports transitional justice and Indigenous people’s rights.

trackers.name: SPDA — Sociedad Peruana de Derecho Ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Peru's leading environmental-law organisation (est. 1986). Runs LITIGIO ESTRATÉGICO in emblematic public-interest cases and operates FREE legal clinics (Consultorios Jurídicos Gratuitos) that have taken on hundreds of cases. WHO IT SUITS: Peruvian communities facing EIA, consulta previa or territorial-defence issues — and environmental or land defenders under threat, who have a dedicated protection programme.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Profonanpe — fondo ambiental del Perú
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Peru's national environmental fund, running Bosques Tropicales — built from the Peru–US debt swap, awarding non-repayable grants — and Conserva Aves calls aimed squarely at creating new subnational protected areas: regional, municipal, communal, indigenous, public or private. WHO IT SUITS: indigenous organisations, native communities and local or regional groups with a recognised record of work with indigenous and local people, plus holders of the various conservation titles; universities qualify only with community participation. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also sub-grants climate finance directly to indigenous organisations, so a federation can hold the money itself.

trackers.name: DAR — Derecho, Ambiente y Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: A Peruvian non-profit working since 2004 on Amazon governance — hydrocarbons, roads, the Hidrovía Amazónica, energy projects and the finance behind them. WHO TO ENLIST for technical and policy backup on consulta previa, environmental impact assessment, the Escazú Agreement and defender protection; it has backed successful court actions brought by indigenous federations, though partner lawyers usually run the litigation. You CAN: use its free guides and consulta-previa protocols, including autonomous protocols written by federations themselves. For activists: strongest while a project is still at the permitting or financing stage, where the leverage is procedure.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is AIDESEP, Asociación Interétnica de Desarrollo de la Selva Peruana — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to AIDESEP first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: FENAMAD — Federación Nativa del Río Madre de Dios y Afluentes
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the indigenous federation of Madre de Dios, running since the mid-1980s and defending the collective rights of Harakbut, Yine, Matsigenka, Ese Eja, Awajún, Kichwa Runa, Amahuaca and Shipibo communities, plus peoples in isolation and initial contact (PIACI), which it has worked on since the mid-1990s. Its practical work is legal security of territory: demarcation, georeferencing and legal recognition of communal land, run with the regional government's land titling directorate, and resizing Bosques de Producción Permanente that overlap communal territory. USE IT: where illegal gold mining or logging is entering titled communal land. It receives confidential satellite monitoring reports from Conservación Amazónica's MAAP project identifying which communities are being invaded. NOTE the domain is fenamad.com.pe, not .org.pe.

trackers.name: Grufides (Cajamarca)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Cajamarca organisation that advises, trains in rights and provides legal defence to communities whose eco-territorial rights are being violated — the region concentrating Peru's largest mining investment and, per the Defensoría del Pueblo, a long-running cluster of socio-environmental conflicts. It brought the amparo in the Conga case and took it to the Latin American Water Tribunal. WHO IT SUITS: campesino communities, rondas and water committees facing a mine, a hydroelectric project or informal mining. It also runs an Observatorio de Conflictos with case files, mining-concession maps and reports naming operators — useful before you have a lawyer at all — and tracks criminalisation of protest, which matters if leaders are already being prosecuted.

trackers.name: PRODHAB — Agencia de Protección de Datos de los Habitantes
trackers.desc: PRODHAB — Agencia de Protección de Datos de los Habitantes — Costa Rica’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: CEDARENA — Centro de Derecho Ambiental y de los Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Costa Rica's environmental and natural-resources law centre, a founding member of AIDA, working on environmental law and land and resource rights. WHO IT SUITS: Costa Rican environmental permitting and land-rights disputes. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as an AIDA founder on aida-americas.org.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Asociación Costa Rica por Siempre
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: administrator of several standing Costa Rican conservation funds — the Fideicomiso Costa Rica por Siempre, SAVIA from the first US debt-for-nature swap, the second swap, and the Fondo Azul — supporting around 45 priority protected areas a year through open convocatorias. WHO IT SUITS: SAVIA calls target social organisations across six regions; the marine window has been open to natural and legal persons, national and foreign, which is unusually wide. HOW IT DIFFERS: an endowment tied to national protected-area commitments, so proposals strengthening a declared área silvestre protegida land best.

trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an ecoregional fund created in 2004 by the national conservation funds of Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, running a Small Grants Program by competitive Call for Proposals — now past its 17th call — with two windows, the Traditional Window and the Reef Rescue Initiative. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. trackers.name: ASJ — Asociación para una Sociedad más Justa (Transparency International Honduras)
trackers.desc: Honduras' national chapter of Transparency International, founded 1998, and one of the few national bodies documenting violence against environmental defenders: with CONADEH it published the 2026 report finding at least 111 environmentalists killed between 2015 and 2025, 92% of those crimes unpunished, and over 30% concentrated in Colón. It runs ALAC Honduras, an Advocacy and Legal Advice Centre that takes citizen corruption complaints - relevant where a concession was granted without the consultation the law required. WHO IT SUITS: communities needing their case documented and escalated rather than litigated; ASJ is a watchdog and advice centre, not a litigator. NOTE: its canonical domain could not be verified this session - reach it through Transparency International's national contacts directory at transparency.org.

trackers.name: Bufete Jurídico Justicia para los Pueblos
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Honduran human-rights law office founded in 2000 by Kenia Oliva and Edy Tabora, combining litigation with investigation and documentation, and working in coordination with social, territorial and trade organisations rather than taking walk-in clients. It defended the Guapinol river defenders of Tocoa against criminalisation, and the Inter-American Commission's Precautionary Measure 137-23 covers the firm itself alongside the Comité Municipal para la Defensa de los Bienes Comunes y Públicos de Tocoa — its lawyers are under threat for this work. WHO IT SUITS: communities and campesino and indigenous leaders facing criminal prosecution brought to clear the way for a mine, dam or plantation. It works through organised movements, so approach with your committee or federation behind you.

trackers.name: Comité Municipal de Defensa de los Bienes Comunes y Públicos de Tocoa
trackers.desc: The community committee at the centre of the Guapinol case: residents of Tocoa organised against the iron-oxide mining concession granted inside the Parque Nacional Montaña de Botaderos 'Carlos Escaleras' and over the ríos Guapinol and San Pedro, the town's water. Eight of its defenders were prosecuted and jailed; two, Aly Domínguez and Jairo Bonilla, were murdered in January 2023, and Óscar Oquelí Domínguez Ramos that June. The Inter-American Commission granted Precautionary Measure 137-23 for its members and their lawyers. WHO IT SUITS: this is a local committee, not a service — it is who you coordinate with if you are in the Aguán or Colón and facing the same concessions, and the template for how a municipal committee holds a national park boundary. NOTE: no canonical domain found; reach it through Bufete Justicia para los Pueblos, its legal representatives, already listed at national level.

trackers.name: Provita
trackers.desc: A Venezuelan non-profit civil association working since 1987, and one of the few conservation bodies still operating nationally. WHO TO ENLIST for two things in particular: it secured the Chacaracual Community Conservation Area on Margarita Island with World Land Trust, so it has done community-held land protection in practice; and since 2021 it co-coordinates Amazonía por la Vida with ORPIA, the regional Indigenous peoples' organisation of Amazonas, strengthening Indigenous territorial governance across Amazonas, Bolívar and Delta Amacuro. You CAN also use its RAISG work: since 2012 it produces the analysis of deforestation, mining, dams, roads and fire pressure on the Venezuelan Amazon, and the Libros Rojos red lists of threatened species and ecosystems.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is ORPIA, Organización Regional de los Pueblos Indígenas de Amazonas — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to ORPIA first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Informacion (ANTAI, Panama)
trackers.desc: Panama's transparency authority, created by Ley 33 de 2013 under the Ley 6 de 2002 transparency regime. You CAN get: a written answer within 30 calendar days, extendable once by up to 30 more only if the request is complex and the official tells you in writing before the first deadline runs out. If the official does not hold the document but knows who does, they are obliged to tell you. If access is refused or ignored, the remedy is an acción de Hábeas Data — and its terms are unusually favourable: ANY person has standing under article 17, and article 19 makes it a summary procedure with no formalities and NO NEED FOR A LAWYER. You CAN'T get: instant compliance — but the penalties are personal to the official, which is rare. An official who defies the tribunal's order is in contempt and fined at least twice their monthly salary, with dismissal for a repeat; one who obstructs access or destroys a record faces the same fine plus administrative and criminal liability; and you may sue them civilly for damages. For activists: use it for concession files, environmental authorisations and inspection records. WHEN NOT TO USE IT: ANTAI itself mediates and supervises — the order comes from a court on habeas data, so if you need compulsion, that is the step that matters.

trackers.name: Fundación Natura (Panamá) — FIDECO, Chagres y Darién
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: administrator of Panama's main environmental trusts — FIDECO, the Fondo Chagres from the country's first debt-for-nature swap in 2003, and the Fondo Darién — with a live Convocatorias page carrying project calls and a capacity-building programme. WHO IT SUITS: NGOs and organizaciones de base comunitaria; the capacity window is deliberately small (recent ceiling US$3,000) and aimed at groups needing institutional footing before a bigger grant. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also runs the donations programme for the state protected-areas system on behalf of MiAmbiente, so some calls are procurement rather than grants — check which.

trackers.name: CIAM — Centro de Incidencia Ambiental de Panamá
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: founded in 2007 by Panamanian civil society, a team of lawyers and environmental and social specialists litigating public-interest environmental cases before national and international tribunals, including the Supreme Court. Its record runs to the attempted reduction of the Donoso protected area, the Cobre Panamá mine, the Remance gold mine impact study, and ministry road routes pushed through with inadequate assessment time. WHO IT SUITS: its legal services are FREE for the communities most affected by environmental harm — that is the door, and it is unusually wide. It accompanies community complaints through administrative environmental processes as well as running strategic litigation, and it prioritises cases that set precedent, so a matter with wider application will get further than a purely local one.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Panama, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. trackers.name: Consorcio Ambiental Dominicano (CAD)
trackers.desc: A membership organisation founded in 1999, made up of around nine state and civil-society institutions and working with more than 40 allied national and international organisations. WHO TO ENLIST as a route into the Dominican environmental sector rather than as a single actor: it convenes specialists across biodiversity, protected areas, sustainable agriculture and coastal-marine ecosystems, and concentrates its work inside protected areas and their buffer zones and along the border zone with Haiti. WHO IT SUITS: communities in or beside a protected area who need technical backing and an introduction to whichever member organisation actually handles their issue. It is a consortium and a technical service network, not a litigator or a grantmaker.

trackers.name: Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (República Dominicana)
trackers.desc: The Dominican environment ministry and the authority for the Sistema Nacional de Áreas Protegidas. You CAN get: the register of protected areas — 131 conservation units in six categories under Ley Sectorial 202-04 as at August 2023, covering 25.32% of the land area and 10.8% of marine waters under Ley 66-07 — downloadable protected-area maps, and the ministry's own lookup services for environmental authorisations, so you can check whether a project near you actually holds one. You CAN'T get: the underlying impact studies as a matter of course, or any guarantee the register is current. For activists: establishing that a project sits inside or beside a declared área protegida, or is operating without an authorisation, is the strongest opening move available here.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. Check whether your country has a national trust fund first — that is usually the door, and the CBF itself is the wholesaler behind it. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign.

trackers.desc: UK ombudsman reporting to Parliament, investigating complaints of maladministration against public bodies.

trackers.name: Woodland Trust — woodland acquisition and protection
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the UK's largest woodland conservation charity — buys threatened woodland and adjoining land outright (funding purchases through public appeals), and campaigns to protect irreplaceable ancient woodland from development. USE IT: if woodland or land next to woodland is at risk of being built on, this is the body that can buy it and the campaign machinery that can fight the application.

trackers.name: John Muir Trust — wild land ownership and community buy-outs
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a conservation charity that protects wild land across the UK both by owning estates directly and by backing community buy-outs of land that comes up for sale. USE IT: for upland, wild and Scottish estate land — they buy, and they put money and weight behind communities trying to buy.

trackers.name: Environmental Law Foundation (ELF)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a UK public-interest environmental law organisation that connects communities and individuals with legal help on environmental and planning matters. WHO IT SUITS: a community or individual affected by a development, a pollution source or the loss of green space, who needs to find out whether there is a legal route at all — and who could run it.

trackers.name: ClientEarth — environmental law charity
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental law charity of roughly 250 lawyers and experts that goes to court to enforce environmental law against governments and companies, with around 168 active cases and offices in London, Brussels, Warsaw, Berlin, Madrid, Beijing and Tokyo. Won the case forcing the UK government to admit it was breaching legal air-pollution limits. WHO IT SUITS: systemic or precedent-setting challenges rather than a single local application — they pick cases that change the rules for everyone.

trackers.name: Rewilding Britain — Rewilding Innovation Fund and buyout support
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Rewilding Innovation Fund has awarded more than half a million pounds to dozens of rewilding initiatives across Britain since 2021, and the charity has put money behind community land buyouts (it helped fund the Langholm crowdfunder). WHO IT SUITS: restoration and rewilding projects in Britain, and communities preparing a buyout. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also publishes the legislation, subsidy and tax guides you need BEFORE taking land out of intensive use — do that homework first.

trackers.name: The Rivers Trust — find your local Rivers Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the umbrella body for 65+ INDEPENDENT member Rivers Trusts across Britain, Northern Ireland and Ireland, each covering its own river catchment. Members restore waterways, run citizen-science monitoring, and drive policy change; the umbrella holds catchment data and expertise. USE IT: the map finds the trust for your catchment. Two reasons to go here rather than to a county body — rivers cross county lines, so a catchment trust may be the only organisation whose remit matches the actual impact area of a development; and they hold long-run water-quality monitoring data, which is documentary evidence a planning objection can rest on. Scotland and Wales have sister bodies (Fisheries Management Scotland, Afonydd Cymru).

trackers.name: National Lottery Heritage Fund — heritage grants
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the UK's largest heritage funder, awarding £10,000 to £10 million across the whole country. NATURE IS EXPLICITLY IN SCOPE — eligible heritage covers natural habitats and landscapes alongside buildings and archives, and funding can pay for capital works, staff posts, professional fees, conservation and volunteer costs. WHO IT SUITS: not-for-profit organisations, partnerships led by one, and — for the £10k–£250k tier only — private owners of a heritage asset who can show significant public benefit. HOW IT DIFFERS: three things decide whether it is worth your time. Applications are ROLLING, not to a deadline. You must bring MATCH FUNDING — at least 5% for grants under £1m, 10% above. And for requests up to £250,000 you can submit a Project Enquiry and get feedback on the idea WITHIN TEN WORKING DAYS, which is the cheapest way to find out if your project fits before writing anything. Note the limit: community sub-grants you pass on to others cannot be used to acquire land.

You CAN get: who holds a permit at a site, its conditions, compliance (CAR) assessments, and the company's enforcement record. You CAN'T get: Scotland (SEPA), Wales (NRW) or Northern Ireland registers — separate systems. For activists: before fighting an incinerator, quarry or discharge pipe, pull the operator's existing permits and breach history — a company already scored for non-compliance is a much easier planning-objection and press story.

Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with the United Kingdom’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: CPRE, the countryside charity — find your local group
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: England's countryside charity (founded 1926, ~40,000 members, around 1,200 volunteers) with more than 200 local groups AND A BRANCH IN EVERY ENGLISH COUNTY. Local groups exist specifically to SHAPE PLANNING DECISIONS, combining local knowledge with national campaigning weight. WHO IT SUITS: anyone facing development on green field, Green Belt or valued landscape in England — this is the nearest thing to an off-the-shelf local ally, and unlike most national bodies you do not need to persuade head office to take an interest. Their track record is the planning system itself: campaigning that led to the Town and Country Planning Act 1947, the National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949, the designation of AONBs, and the Green Belt circular. Current campaigns cover Green Belt, hedgerows, dark skies and rural affordable housing — useful if you need to frame an objection in policy terms rather than local feeling.

trackers.name: The Wildlife Trusts — find your county Wildlife Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a federation of 46–47 INDEPENDENT COUNTY-BASED charities covering the UK, Isle of Man and Alderney — each one its own registered charity for its county, not a branch. Between them they own and manage more than 2,600 nature reserves over roughly 112,000 hectares plus 10,120 km of watercourse, with over 945,000 members. USE IT: the map finds the trust for your county. The reason they matter against development is ownership — almost all are significant landowners and COLLECTIVELY THE THIRD LARGEST VOLUNTARY-SECTOR LANDOWNER IN THE UK — so a county trust can take land on, hold a reserve adjoining your site, or object as an affected neighbouring landowner rather than merely as a consultee. Being independent charities, they can also campaign locally without waiting for national sign-off.

trackers.name: The Langholm Initiative — community buyout (worked example)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY (worked example): the development trust behind south Scotland's largest community buyout — roughly £6 million raised across TWO buyouts to purchase a 4,249 ha former grouse moor from Buccleuch Estates, stacking a public crowdfunder, a £1m Scottish Land Fund award, philanthropic donors and charities including John Muir Trust, Woodland Trust, RSPB Scotland and Rewilding Britain. WHO IT SUITS: a community that wants to BUY the land rather than object to what happens to it. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is a template, not a funder — study how the funding stack was assembled.

trackers.name: Scottish Land Fund
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a grant fund established under Scotland's land reform legislation that supports COMMUNITY PURCHASES of land and assets — it awarded £1 million toward the Langholm buyout. WHO IT SUITS: Scottish communities where the answer to a threatened site is for the community to own it. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is public money with a statutory basis, not philanthropy — usually the anchor of a buyout funding stack. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; documented on rewildingbritain.org.uk and rewild.scot.

trackers.name: Borders Forest Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Scottish land-owning conservation charity — took ownership of the 655 ha Carrifran valley and has planted close to a million trees there, and backed the Langholm community buyout. USE IT: a southern-Scotland acquirer and restoration partner for degraded upland. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as a partner on rewildingbritain.org.uk.

trackers.name: Environmental Rights Centre for Scotland (ERCS)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Scottish charity (SCIO SC050257) running SCOTLAND'S ONLY FREE ADVICE SERVICE on environmental and planning law — over 325 enquiries answered — and using public interest litigation to hold public bodies to account when advice is not enough. It is in the process of establishing its own law firm to become Scotland's first law centre for environmental justice. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Scotland facing a worrying planning application, loss of greenspace, pollution, or a refused request for environmental information — Scots law and the Scottish planning system differ from England's, so this is the correct first call north of the border, not an English body.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Scotland
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Scottish campaigning organisation working on environmental rights and access to justice, which has taken big polluters to court — including defending Scotland's fracking ban when INEOS sought to overturn it — and campaigns for full Scottish compliance with the Aarhus Convention on participation, information and access to justice. WHO IT SUITS: communities wanting campaign support and rights expertise alongside legal help; for the legal advice itself, go to ERCS.

trackers.name: Wildlife Trusts Wales — planning and development in Wales
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Welsh federation of Wildlife Trusts, which works on development in the wrong place and publishes a plain guide to the Welsh planning system. USE THE GUIDE FIRST: planning is DEVOLVED, so Wales has its own primary legislation (Planning (Wales) Act 2015) and its own policy stack — Planning Policy Wales (PPW11), Future Wales: The National Plan 2040, and Technical Advice Note 5 on nature conservation — which local planning authorities must comply with. English planning guidance does not apply here, and citing it will weaken your objection. Their key argument: all development in Wales must now deliver a NET BENEFIT FOR BIODIVERSITY.

trackers.name: Future Generations Commissioner for Wales
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a politically independent statutory Commissioner created by the Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015, which requires Welsh PUBLIC BODIES to act in pursuit of long-term well-being in accordance with the sustainable development principle. The Commissioner may advise and assist those bodies and advise the Auditor General for Wales on sustainable development. USE IT: this duty has no equivalent in England or Scotland — if a Welsh council, Natural Resources Wales or another public body is backing a damaging project, the Act gives you a distinct line of attack on HOW the decision was reached, and a Commissioner whose remit is to press them on exactly that.

trackers.name: Welsh Government — environmental regulators in Wales (signposting guide)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Welsh Government's own directory of who regulates what in Wales — Natural Resources Wales for air, land, water and intensive farming; Cadw for the historic environment and scheduled monument consent; the Agricultural Land Tribunal for Wales for tenancy, drainage and land-improvement disputes; plus animal, plant and fish health bodies. USE IT: to work out which body you actually complain to or request records from before you spend effort on the wrong one.

trackers.name: Local Places for Nature Capital Fund (Wales)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Welsh Government and Heritage Fund priority programme for nature recovery, aimed specifically at nature 'FROM YOUR DOORSTEP' — where people live, work, access services and spend leisure time, rather than remote landscapes. WHO IT SUITS: not-for-profit organisations, statutory and third sector, with a bank account and a constitution; pre-application advice is available by email before you commit. HOW IT DIFFERS: 85% of the scheme is CAPITAL funding, and there is a hard catch — capital money MAY NOT BE USED TO LEASE LAND, so any proposal built around a lease is likely ineligible. You must also show you can maintain the asset long term. For grants between £100,000 and £250,000, contact them by email before proceeding.

trackers.name: Environmental Justice Network Ireland (EJNI)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a network working on environmental justice across the ISLAND OF IRELAND — both Northern Ireland and the Republic — publishing joint legal and policy submissions with Community Law & Mediation's Centre for Environmental Justice. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Northern Ireland, where environmental enforcement has historically been weak and Brexit removed the European Commission's enforcement route, leaving a recognised accountability gap. Cross-border sites are its natural fit, since it works to both jurisdictions rather than only one.

trackers.name: UVP-Verbund — federal/state EIA portal network
trackers.desc: Germany's joint federal-state portal for environmental impact assessments (UVP): the official publication point for assessment procedures, documents, and decisions across the Bund and Länder. You CAN get: which projects are undergoing UVP near you, the application documents and decisions, and the consultation timelines that set your objection (Einwendung) deadlines. You CAN'T get: a machine-readable API — it's built for reading, not harvesting. For activists: German participation rights hinge on filing objections within the consultation window; this portal is where the clock and the documents live, and recognized environmental associations gain litigation standing (Verbandsklage) from participating.

trackers.name: NABU-Stiftung Nationales Naturerbe — Naturschutz durch Landkauf
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a German foundation (established 2002, seat in Berlin) whose central method is BUYING conservation land — over 16,200 hectares now in its care, plus around 8,800 hectares across 157 protected areas taken over from the federal Nationales Naturerbe pool. It builds endowment capital (Stiftungskapital) alongside the land so running costs are met from investment income, making the holdings independent of year-to-year donations. USE IT: two routes. Propose a threatened site for purchase; or check whether the land is federally owned, because since 2005 the Bund no longer commercially privatises nationally significant conservation land and instead transfers it FREE OF CHARGE to Länder and conservation bodies — roughly 220,000 ha since 2003. If your site sits in that pool, the fight is about designation, not price.

trackers.name: UfU — Unabhängiges Institut für Umweltfragen (Umweltrecht & Partizipation)
trackers.desc: Germany's independent environmental-science institute and citizens' organisation, founded in East Berlin in 1990, with a standing department for environmental law and public participation. WHO TO ENLIST for the mechanics of getting heard: access to courts in environmental matters and Öffentlichkeitsbeteiligung are core profile areas, and it runs a dedicated participation portal alongside its studies. You CAN: draw on applied research written for citizens rather than for ministries, on how participation rights actually work in German procedures. For activists: the evidence base and the procedural map — this is a research institute, so expect analysis and training, not representation in your case.

trackers.name: Bewegungsstiftung — Förderung für Kampagnen und Bewegungsarbeit
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a German community foundation that funds protest itself — campaigns, not charity — across four programmes running from about €3,000 to €100,000, plus up to €3,000 towards paid external advice on facilitation, fundraising or press work. Around €6M to social movements since 2002, including anti-coal campaigning and resistance to villages being demolished for lignite mining. WHO IT SUITS: an initiative with a medium- or long-term campaign strategy, not a one-off event. For tax reasons most programmes require recognised gemeinnützig status — but an unincorporated initiative group CAN apply jointly with a registered gemeinnütziger Verein, which becomes the formal recipient, so lacking legal form is not a bar. HOW IT DIFFERS: funders that exclude political and awareness campaigning are the norm; this one exists for exactly that.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is UfU, the Independent Institute for Environmental Issues. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on UfU, the Independent Institute for Environmental Issues's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do.

trackers.name: NRW-Stiftung — Objektförderung und Flächenerwerb
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the state foundation for North Rhine-Westphalia, which both funds and buys. Its Objektförderung pays for securing land that is under nature or landscape protection OR merely suitable for it — so a threatened parcel does not need to be designated already — and its Projektförderung covers everything from a few hundred euros for a publication or a management measure up to large schemes. It has secured about 7,500 hectares by purchase and holds roughly 7,057 hectares outright, spending around €300M since 1986. WHO IT SUITS: local voluntary initiatives and charitable associations with a project rooted in NRW. Involving volunteer effort is a stated precondition of funding, and an application needs a coherent cost and financing plan plus your own contribution. HOW IT DIFFERS: most funders will not buy the land — this one will.

trackers.name: BUND NRW Naturschutzstiftung — Flächenankauf
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys land worth protecting in North Rhine-Westphalia and holds it as foundation property, which secures it permanently — the foundation is constituted 'for ever', charitable, and politically and financially independent. It has bought valley woodland in the Siebengebirge and old orchard parcels near Bornheim, and has accepted woodland by gift where a local BUND group initiated it. USE IT: but note the condition it states openly — it buys when the purchase makes conservation sense AND the local BUND group is willing and able to take on the necessary ongoing management of the site voluntarily. So find and commit the local group first; without people to mow the meadow, the purchase will not happen.

trackers.name: Bayerischer Naturschutzfonds
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Bavaria's state nature foundation, set up in 1982 as an independent foundation under public law, which funds the purchase or long-term lease of ecologically valuable land as well as biotope works, project management, applied research and public outreach. It separately administers the Ersatzgelder held by the lower nature-conservation authorities. WHO IT SUITS: both natural and legal persons may apply, but in practice the project carriers are conservation and landscape-management associations and municipalities, and they carry an own contribution of 15 to 50 percent — so budget for your share before you ask. Two screens that reject applications: it funds discrete projects only and gives no institutional or core funding, and it will not fund anything you are legally obliged to do, including compensation and replacement measures under the Bavarian nature conservation act. HOW IT DIFFERS: it stands behind the state's own programmes rather than beside them — if a Bavarian state funding scheme could cover your measure, check that route first, because the foundation will point you there.

trackers.name: Niedersächsische Bingo-Umweltstiftung
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Lower Saxony's environmental foundation, funded from the gambling levy and the Bingo environmental lottery, which funds practical conservation work explicitly as a complement to the state's statutory duties — creating new biotopes and ecologically upgrading existing ones, biotope networking, margin habitats along paths and watercourses, wet fallows, avenues, Wallhecken and field copses. Its stated principles are sustainability, VOLUNTEER involvement and practicality, so a project with real hands behind it beats a polished one without. WHO IT SUITS: tax-privileged bodies and bodies under public law only — registered associations, foundations, charitable companies, municipalities, schools. Private individuals cannot apply, and the applicant must hold its tax seat in Lower Saxony, proven with a Freistellungsbescheid from a Lower Saxony tax office. HOW IT DIFFERS: it publishes a routing rule. Applications up to €30,000 can come straight here; above that, ask NBank first whether your project fits a state programme. Separately, the Emsfonds is earmarked money for the ecological state of the Ems-Dollart region and is the one pot not tied to a Lower Saxony seat.

trackers.name: Stiftung Naturschutzfonds Baden-Württemberg
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a statutory foundation under public law, set up in 1976 under the Baden-Württemberg Naturschutzgesetz, which has backed more than 3,900 projects. Two streams, and the second is the one to understand. Ersatzzahlungen are the sums paid to the foundation as compensation for interventions in nature and landscape — and they are earmarked for practical conservation measures IN THE NATURRAUM THE INTERVENTION AFFECTED. So the money a developer paid for wrecking your area is legally tied to your area, and you can apply for it. WHO IT SUITS: unusually wide — charitable organisations, municipal bodies, universities, other organisations and PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS can all apply. Land purchase counts as a fundable project-related investment where it implements a measure. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications up to €50,000 are taken on a rolling basis and normally decided within three months; larger ones wait for the Stiftungsrat's cycle, so size your ask deliberately.

trackers.name: Stiftung NaturSchutzFonds Brandenburg
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Land foundation whose statutory task is practical nature conservation, funded mainly by Ersatzzahlungen under § 15 BbgNatSchG — the sums paid by those who seal soil or erect wind turbines and masts — plus lottery proceeds. It steers that money back into the very districts where the damage was caused, and its council gives particular priority to projects in municipalities that took in Ersatzzahlungen from wind-energy impacts. So if a wind farm went up near you, there is money with your district's name on it. WHO IT SUITS: anyone. Any legal or natural person — district, municipality, private individual, association or society — may apply, and funding land purchase BY THIRD PARTIES is one of its three acquisition routes. Two constraints to plan around: land bought with Ersatzzahlung must have improvement potential the purchase can realise, so already-pristine ground does not qualify, and it will not fund recurring maintenance, anything you are legally obliged to do, or work already begun. HOW IT DIFFERS: its grants are recognised as your own contribution under EU, federal and Land schemes, so a euro from here can pull in roughly two and a half.

trackers.name: Stiftung Naturschutz Schleswig-Holstein (Stiftungsland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a foundation under public law, created by the Land in 1978 and anchored in the Landesnaturschutzgesetz, whose statutory task is to secure land for nature conservation — and whose most important instrument, alongside long-term leasing, is outright purchase, because that is often the only way to hold a valuable biotope. It now holds over 35,000 hectares, more than one percent of the whole Land. The money for buying comes largely from levies and compensation payments, so it is the developer's mitigation money that funds it. USE IT: two doors, and the second is the one communities miss. You can sell or donate land to the foundation directly. But it ALSO funds the purchase of suitable land BY OTHER BODIES — municipalities and nature-conservation associations — so a parish council or a local Verein can be the buyer with the foundation paying. On peatland it has run a Klimapunkte model that buys rewetting rights rather than the land, priced on tonnes of CO2 avoided over thirty years and often paying more than a straight sale; ask whether it is currently open, as it began as a time-limited trial.

trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); MaDada — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Conservatoire du littoral — acquisition foncière (coastal land purchase)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a French public body that BUYS coastal and lakeshore land to protect it permanently — about 70% by negotiated purchase, 26% by pre-emption (right of first refusal, alongside the SAFER or the département), and rarely by expropriation. Land it acquires enters an inalienable public domain and cannot be sold on. In 2025 it covered roughly 750 sites and 203,762 hectares. USE IT: if the threatened land is near the coast or a large lake, the pre-emption right is the sharpest tool in France — alert them BEFORE a sale completes.

trackers.name: Fédération des Conservatoires d'espaces naturels (FCEN)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the national federation (created 1988) of France's 23 Conservatoires d'espaces naturels — nature-protection associations whose whole method is MAÎTRISE FONCIÈRE ET D'USAGE: acquiring land, or securing use rights over it, to protect it. Together they hold or manage a network of more than 3,300 sites covering roughly 161,000 hectares, and since the Grenelle II law of 2010 they can be formally approved by the State and the regions. USE IT: to find the CEN covering your département via the federation's directory, and to propose a threatened site for acquisition or a long-term management agreement — the CENs also lease, not only buy, which can be faster than a purchase.

trackers.name: Terre de Liens — Foncière (citizen-funded farmland acquisition)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys farmland and farm buildings outright using citizen solidarity savings — shares from about €106, with a 25% tax reduction — and commits never to resell, permanently removing the land from speculation and leasing it to organic and peasant farmers. Backed by a network of regional associations across metropolitan France plus a public-utility foundation that accepts land donations. USE IT: if farmland near you is about to be sold to a developer, or you need land for a farming project — every acquisition is tied to an identified, assessed project, so bring the farmer as well as the parcel.

trackers.name: France Nature Environnement — fédération et pôle juridique
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the federation of roughly 9,000 French nature-protection associations, reconnue d'utilité publique since 1976, which litigates in its own name — it took the Water Framework Directive deterioration question to the CJEU and won, challenged the neonicotinoid derogation before the administrative courts, and has complained to the Aarhus Committee that France obstructs associations' access to justice. WHO IT SUITS: read this first if you are forming a group. Under article L. 600-1-1 of the Code de l'urbanisme, as amended by the ELAN law, an association can only challenge an urbanism authorisation if it filed its statutes at least ONE YEAR before the authorisation application was posted — so file now, not when the bulldozers appear. Its 46 member federations are also the route to a local ally already holding the agrément that carries standing.

trackers.name: SAFER — droit de préemption et veille foncière (Vigifoncier)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: holds two statutory powers over French rural land. A droit d'information under article L. 141-1-1 of the Code rural obliges the notaire to notify the SAFER of every transfer of rural property, land or farm — sale, gift, exchange or contribution to a company — at least two months before the final deed. A droit de préemption under article L. 143-1 then lets it buy in place of the original purchaser, resell at a state-approved price after a call for candidates, and attach a cahier des charges with environmental clauses that binds the new owner. USE IT: the early warning is the real prize. Notifications are published on the Vigifoncier portal, geolocated, with price, area, cadastral reference and the parties, and layers for water catchments, espaces naturels sensibles and wetlands. Access runs through collectivités that sign a veille foncière convention — so the route for a community group is via its commune, which can also stand as a candidate to buy. Individuals with a serious agricultural project can write to the departmental Conseiller Foncier while a notification is live. Two limits: pre-emption is exercised on only a small minority of notified sales, and purely forestry property is outside it.

trackers.desc: Transparency International's Italy chapter (30+ years). Anti-corruption research, education and advocacy; runs an Advocacy and Legal Advice Centre (ALAC) for victims and witnesses of corruption; and helps citizens and organisations obtain public data.

trackers.name: FAI — Fondo per l'Ambiente Italiano (donate land or property)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Italy's national trust, founded 1975 on the British National Trust model, which takes ownership or long-term concession of buildings, gardens and fragile natural habitats and protects them permanently, opening them to the public. It accepts land and property by donation in life, by bequest, or by concession, and runs its own conservation department. USE IT: if you own or can direct a threatened parcel — gifts and inheritances to FAI are exempt from succession and donation tax and from the imposta ipotecaria and catastale, so the whole value reaches the protection. Property that FAI cannot itself hold can be donated and sold to fund work elsewhere, so a non-scenic parcel is still worth offering.

trackers.name: Legambiente — Osservatorio Ambiente e Legalità / Ecomafia
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Italy's largest environmental association, which says plainly on its own legality page how it fights — by constituting itself parte civile in criminal trials, and by appealing to the regional administrative courts (TAR) and the Consiglio di Stato against unlawful and damaging administrative measures. It coined the term ecomafia in 1994 and publishes the annual Ecomafia report through its Osservatorio Ambiente e Legalità, which tracks the ciclo del cemento — abusivismo edilizio, illegal quarries, rigged public-works contracts — region by region and names the cases. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing illegal or corrupt construction, quarrying or waste dumping, where the route is a criminal prosecution you can attach to rather than a permit challenge you must bring alone.

trackers.name: Corte dei conti
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Italy, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.desc: Italy's national VAS-VIA-AIA portal for state-competence environmental assessment and authorisation under Part Two of Legislative Decree 152/2006 (run by the environment ministry, now MASE; a platform migration is under way). You CAN get: technical documents for projects under national evaluation and the concluding acts issued since 1989, plus the 45-day public-comment windows. You CAN'T get: regional-competence procedures handled by the Regions. For activists: track a national project's file and file observations during the consultation window.

trackers.name: Sir[a]
trackers.desc: Sir[a] originated from the Community Action Group, a grassroots organisation working on mental health and human rights. It is a centre for holistic medical, psychological, and legal care for people affected by situations of violence, mistreatment, or torture. Its headquarters are in Madrid, with a presence in Barcelona, the Basque Country and Valencia. Staff members are professionals in psychiatry, psychology, medicine, law, and journalism, including with high-level expertise on the Istanbul Protocol. Sir[a] works to support processes of justice and reparation, including rehabilitation through a human rights, psychosocial and cross-cultural approach. Around 80% of the referrals it receives are of people who suffered ill-treatment and torture. Its work includes lawsuits for ill-treatment and torture in Spain but also for other courts, such as the European Court of Human Rights or the International Criminal Court. In addition to individual cases, Sir[a] carries out expert reports on collective cases of human rights violations and torture at the international level. It also has a research area dedicated to the implementation of innovative tools for the documentation of torture, the credibility of allegations and impact assessment.

trackers.name: Maldita.es (investigative outlet)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (investigative newsroom); Maldita.es (investigative outlet) — Spanish fact-checking and data-journalism newsroom holding power to account, exposing disinformation and using FOI to force transparency.

trackers.name: IIDMA — Instituto Internacional de Derecho y Medio Ambiente
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Spain's nonprofit environmental law centre, founded 1996 and declared of public utility, which puts law at the service of the environment through litigation before public administrations and the courts — most Spanish environmental cases run through the contencioso-administrativo or criminal jurisdictions, and IIDMA works in both. Accredited to the UN Environment Assembly since 1998 and a member of the Justice and Environment network, so it also pursues EU-level routes. WHO IT SUITS: a group with a case that can move Spanish or EU environmental law, rather than a routine neighbour dispute — this is a strategic-litigation and policy centre, not a walk-in advice desk.

trackers.name: Plataforma de Custodia del Territorio (Fundación Biodiversidad)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the state-level meeting point for Spain's custodia del territorio movement, run by the Fundación Biodiversidad under the environment ministry. Custodia is a statutory mechanism: article 76 of the Ley de Patrimonio Natural y de la Biodiversidad obliges public administrations to promote voluntary agreements between accredited custodia entities and owners of private OR public land whose main object is conserving natural heritage, and lets the State cede management of its own land in natural spaces to those entities. Publishes the national inventory of custodia agreements and entities. USE IT: to find the custodia entity that can take on a threatened finca near you, or to push a municipality to sign as an owner or as an entity itself — hundreds of agreements already sit on public land.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is IIDMA. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on IIDMA's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do.

trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Czech public-interest law NGO whose counselling centre answers over 500 queries a year, free, with an emphasis on environmental protection, maladministration and clientelism — and which publishes model legal submissions, FAQs and manuals online so you can file yourself. Works on both Czech and Polish cases from offices in Brno, Ostrava, Prague, Kraków and Brussels; long record on coal, air quality and permit proceedings. WHO IT SUITS: an individual or a local initiative being shut out of an administrative proceeding or refused information by an authority. trackers.name: ČSOP — Místo pro přírodu (land-purchase collection & pozemkové spolky)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys land to stop it being destroyed, using a registered public collection rather than an endowment. Místo pro přírodu has run since 2003 and has purchased 218 hectares at 61 sites — near-natural woodland, wetlands, steppe, flower-rich meadows, and ground along watercourses earmarked for restoration. Bought land becomes ČSOP's own property and is then handed to a local pozemkový spolek, a land trust, to care for permanently. USE IT three ways. Donate and CHOOSE THE SITE — the collection lets a giver pick which of dozens of locations their money buys, so a community can point outside support at its own parcel. Bring it a site: recent purchases include a hectare added to the Sedmihorské mokřady wetland and three hectares of floodplain forest near Karviná, both prompted locally. Or start your own land trust — ČSOP publishes the founding stories of existing pozemkové spolky as a how-to, and ownership is often the only durable way to protect ground that designation alone has failed to save.

trackers.name: Pozemkové spolky — Czech land trust network and purchase procedure
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the network of Czech land trusts, which take on care of natural and historic sites by agreement with the owner and, where agreement is not enough, by purchase — and unusually, it publishes the actual procedure instead of an invitation to get in touch. USE IT: the sequence is the point. You can apply to have a locality accepted into the purchase campaign BEFORE any negotiation, so the National Land Trust Council rules on whether the site qualifies before you approach the owner, and a Council member or central-office officer visits it before the application is decided. A second application follows once a specific parcel is agreed with the owner. The local land trust does the negotiating; the central office drafts the contract. Two things worth taking from their own guidance: gather everything you can about the site and, where you do not have a fact, say so rather than write an unverified assumption. And if no land trust covers your area, the site sets out how to found one.

trackers.desc: Statutory provider of civil legal aid and advice in Ireland. · Find here: civil (and some criminal) legal aid in Ireland (Legal Aid Board).

trackers.name: Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; Ireland’s Office of the Information Commissioner is the independent appeals body under the Freedom of Information Act 2014 — reviewing public-body FOI decisions (affirm, vary or annul) and publishing binding decisions, Ireland.

trackers.name: Community Law & Mediation — Centre for Environmental Justice
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an independent community law centre and charity (working since 1975) providing FREE legal advice, representation and mediation, which opened a dedicated Centre for Environmental Justice in 2021 — launched by Mary Robinson — staffed with an environmental justice lawyer. Runs a free legal advice clinic, publishes a guide to the Aarhus Convention, and produces template consultation responses communities can adapt. WHO IT SUITS: Irish communities impacted by social exclusion or disadvantage where an environmental harm falls hardest — that equality framing is the centre's explicit remit, so lead with who is being affected, not only with what is being built.

trackers.name: An Taisce — The National Trust for Ireland
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ireland's oldest environmental NGO (provisional 1946, incorporated 1948), a statutory consultee in the Irish planning system that also brings judicial review against An Bord Pleanála — including the Edenderry Peat case (An Taisce v Bord na Móna [2020] IESC 39), which established that an EIA had to consider the impacts of extracting the plant's peat feedstock, and the Kilkenny Cheese challenge. Currently challenging, with Friends of the Irish Environment, the Planning and Development (Costs of Part 9 Judicial Review Proceedings) Regulations 2026 as breaching the Aarhus Convention and EU law. WHO IT SUITS: Irish planning and habitats challenges with national significance. NOTE: canonical domain not verified this session.

trackers.name: Friends of the Irish Environment (FIE)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Irish environmental NGO that litigates in the superior courts — it brought Friends of the Irish Environment v Ireland [2020] IESC 49, 'Climate Case Ireland', in which the Supreme Court quashed the Government's national mitigation plan, and it litigates jointly with An Taisce on planning and access-to-justice matters. WHO IT SUITS: strategic challenges to State plans and policies rather than a single local application. USEFUL TO KNOW: under s.50A(3) of the Planning and Development Act 2000 as amended, an environmental organisation does NOT need to be incorporated or registered to bring a planning judicial review in Ireland, and after the Heather Hill judgment environmental litigants are generally liable only for their OWN costs — an unusually open door, though the 2026 costs regulations are narrowing it. NOTE: canonical domain not verified this session.

trackers.name: NPWS — about the National Parks and Wildlife Service
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the State agency for nature conservation, within the Heritage Division of the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage. Its remit covers designation of Natural Heritage Areas, Special Areas of Conservation and Special Protection Areas under the Habitats and Birds Directives; licensing under the Wildlife Acts; peatland policy, turf compensation and relocation; land designation and land restoration; and management of State-owned National Parks and Nature Reserves. USE IT: to work out which designation, if any, already applies to a threatened site and who inside the Department holds that file — designation status changes what a developer must prove.

trackers.name: NPWS — useful links directory for Irish nature bodies
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the State conservation agency's own list of the organisations that matter for Irish nature — An Taisce (the National Trust for Ireland), Coillte (the State forestry company), BirdWatch Ireland, the Heritage Council, Bat Conservation Ireland, the Irish Whale and Dolphin Group, the National Biodiversity Data Centre and the Irish Ramsar Wetlands Committee. USE IT: a government-maintained starting point for finding the specialist body for your habitat or species, and a way to confirm an organisation is the real one rather than a soundalike.

trackers.name: Coillte Nature Trust — funded native woodland creation
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Nature Trust raised over EUR 7 million from external funders to create 650 hectares of new native woodland in Ireland, and has transferred the established woodlands to An Taisce to hold and manage long term. WHO IT SUITS: restoration and native-woodland creation projects rather than defensive campaigns. HOW IT DIFFERS: it is a worked model of the corporate-funded creation plus NGO long-term stewardship split — useful as a template for structuring a similar deal, and as evidence that Coillte land can move into conservation hands.

trackers.name: Irish Wildlife Trust — find your county branch
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ireland's nature conservation charity and lobbyist (since 1979), with branches that organise conservation activity IN THEIR COUNTY — Dublin, Cork, Galway, Kerry, Waterford, Cavan, Laois/Offaly and Longford/Westmeath among them. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing development who wants people locally rather than a Dublin office. BE REALISTIC: branch coverage is partial, and the IWT describes itself as a single nationwide organisation rather than a federation of independent county bodies — so a branch is a route to the national organisation, not a separate local charity with its own resources. It has a campaigning record on habitat protection, including opposing the 2017 Heritage Bill provisions extending hedge-cutting and scrub-burning into the bird breeding season.

trackers.name: BirdWatch Ireland — local branches
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ireland's largest independent conservation organisation (est. 1968, over 15,000 members) with a network of more than 30 branches nationwide — the widest local conservation coverage in the country. It also manages nature reserves and works with the National Biodiversity Data Centre on wildlife monitoring. WHO IT SUITS: any Irish site where birds or their habitats are affected. THE PRACTICAL VALUE IS EVIDENCE: a branch with local recording history can supply documented species records for a threatened site, which carries far more weight in a planning objection than an assertion that birds use the land.

trackers.name: Irish Environmental Network — member directory
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the umbrella body for 34 of Ireland's national environmental NGOs, with a directory describing what each one does — An Taisce, BirdWatch Ireland, the Irish Wildlife Trust, Bat Conservation Ireland, CELT and others. USE IT: Ireland has no county-level conservation trusts, so finding the right national specialist is the equivalent step. Work down this list to find the organisation whose specific remit matches your site — bats, birds, water, woodland — because a specialist body carries more weight on its own subject than a general one.

trackers.name: The Rivers Trust — member trusts in Ireland
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the same 65-member network extends to the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland, and its Irish members are INDEPENDENT LOCAL CHARITIES, not branches of a national body — the Maigue Rivers Trust in County Limerick, for example, runs its own catchment programmes with National Biodiversity Action Plan and LAWPRO Community Water Development Fund money. USE IT: this is the exception to the general Irish pattern. Ireland has no county conservation trusts, but it does have catchment-based river trusts with their own funding and their own staff — so if your site is in a river catchment, there may be a genuinely local organisation after all. Check the member map before assuming there is nothing nearby.

trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: co-founds and works with small-grants funds that pass money from large donors down to grassroots groups and environmental and human-rights defenders — often only a few thousand euros, with the recipient deciding what it is spent on. WHO IT SUITS: a local group that would never survive an international application cycle. HOW IT DIFFERS: decisions are made by the regional fund, not a distant donor, and can move fast enough to get a threatened defender to safety.

trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the Netherlands' largest nature-conservation membership association (founded 1905, 968,000 members), which BUYS and manages land — over 112,000 hectares across some 355 reserves. Its stated strategy is to purchase ground both to create new nature and to CONNECT existing fragmented reserves. USE IT: Dutch land under threat that adjoins or bridges an existing reserve is exactly their acquisition priority — make that connectivity argument when you approach them.

trackers.name: Stichting DOEN — grants and loans for green initiatives
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the fund of the Dutch Postcode Loterij and VriendenLoterij, giving both grants and loans to front-runner initiatives — including citizens' collectives (burgercollectieven) working on landscape restoration and regenerative agriculture. Lends where banks will not, because applicants cannot offer security, and recycles repayments into new green and social initiatives. WHO IT SUITS: a legal person only — applications from individuals are not considered — with a costed SMART plan, past the research stage and into pilot or early rollout. Organisations already holding sufficient reserves are excluded. Apply any time, but at least four months before the project starts; the procedure takes about four months. HOW IT DIFFERS: purely political or awareness campaigns are excluded, so this funds the alternative you are building, not the fight against the development.

trackers.name: Nationaal Groenfonds — leningen voor groene projecten
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Dutch green financing institution, lending into nature and landscape, water, sustainable agriculture, circular economy and climate adaptation — including, in some cases, subordinated debt or equity. WHO IT SUITS: read this before spending an afternoon on it, because the screen is hard. It lends to organisations and enterprises ONLY and states flatly on its own front page that it NEVER provides loans, subsidies or payments to private individuals, not even through intermediaries. The minimum loan is €200,000 apart from its sustainable-agriculture fund, security such as a mortgage charge may be required, and it funds only projects with a demonstrable return for the green environment. HOW IT DIFFERS: it gives no grants at all. This is debt. It is the right instrument for a land trust or a foundation buying ground it can service, and the wrong one for a residents' campaign.

trackers.name: Naturskyddsföreningen — talerätt och kretsar
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Sweden's largest environmental association, founded 1909, and the practical route to the statutory right of appeal. Under 16 kap. 13 § miljöbalken a non-profit association whose statutes give it the purpose of protecting nature or the environment may appeal decisions granting permits, approvals and dispensations under the Environmental Code — but the section sets minimum thresholds for membership and years of operation that exclude most local groups in practice. WHO IT SUITS: a neighbourhood group that does not itself qualify. The association's kretsar and länsförbund do, and there is case law where a länsförbund took over a local krets's action by power of attorney after the krets was found to fall short. Bring the case to them rather than filing alone and being dismissed on standing.
